title: How to Find Process Service Invoices and Returns on Ody's Website
summary: Where to find the return of service and the invoice for a process server job on the process server's website, step by step, instead of emailing for them.
body:
Ody Process is the process server the firm uses to serve defendants. When the firm asks Ody for the invoice or the return of service on an old job, Ody answers that both are available much faster on its website. Use the steps below instead of emailing for them.

### Find a return of service or invoice on Ody's website

1. Go to **odyprocess.com**.
2. Click **Web Tracking**.
3. Scroll down to the **red box** to avoid the cookies notice.
4. Sign in with the firm's Ody username and password. These are not stored here. Ask your supervisor or the litigation point of contact for them.
5. You are now on the **Dashboard**. You can sort the jobs by name, case and so on.
6. Click the **blue numbers** (Ody's job number) to see every detail about the service.
7. At the bottom of the page you will see the **return of service** and the **invoice**, if the job is closed.

### Tips

- Check the dashboard first for any return of service or invoice on an old job, before you email Ody.
- File the return of service in the case file, and give the invoice to the paralegal or accountant who handles process server payments.
- If a job is not closed, the return and the invoice will not be there yet. Follow up on the return of service as described in *Litigation Procedure 2: Service of Pleadings*.

title: Litigation Procedure 1: Initiation of the Lawsuit
summary: The first step to initiate the litigation process is the drafting and filing of the complaint and summons. Part of the firm’s strategy during the initiation of the lawsuit, is also the drafting and filing of plain…
body:
### Initiation of the lawsuit – Complaint, Summons, Plaintiff Disco to Def and Initial Plaintiff’s Deposition request of defendant - (For Paralegals ONLY)

The first step to initiate the litigation process is the drafting and filing of the complaint and summons. Part of the firm’s strategy during the initiation of the lawsuit, is also the drafting and filing of plaintiff’s discovery request to defendant. **Note:** if the lawsuit was filed in the wrong county, there will be an order to transfer action which has to be done within 30 days of the order, otherwise, the case will be dismissed without prejudice (Please refer to Rule 1.060.0). Brief description of this phase terminology below along with all steps to draft all documents necessary to initiate the lawsuit:

  1. **General term’s definition:**

- Complaint:

Formal Lawsuit - Unlike criminal cases, which are initiated by the government, a formal personal injury case typically starts when a private individual (the "plaintiff") files a civil complaint against another person, business, corporation, or government agency (the "defendant"), alleging that they acted carelessly or irresponsibly in connection with an accident or injury that caused harm. This action is known as "filing a lawsuit"

- Summons:

An order signed and stamped by clerk or judge to appear before a judge.

- Case Management Plan:

It is a comprehensive order issued by the judge reflecting all pretrial case management deadlines, and, if applicable, a trial setting and pretrial compliance requirements. In other words, it is what defines all deadlines that must be followed throughout the litigation process which must be calendared as soon as a complaint is filed.

- Discovery request:

This involves asking the opposing party or other people to provide information that would not be publicly known or readily available to the party seeking it. This is the part in which both parties start gathering all their evidence to prepare for a potential trial.

- Deposition:

A deposition is a [witness's](https://www.law.cornell.edu/wex/witness#:~:text=A%20witness%20is%20someone%20with,the%20first%20signature%20is%20genuine.) sworn out-of-court [testimony](https://www.law.cornell.edu/wex/testimony#:~:text=Testimony%20is%20oral%20or%20written,trial%20or%20other%20legal%20procedures.). It is used to gather information as part of the [discovery](https://www.law.cornell.edu/wex/discovery) process and, in limited circumstances, may be used at [trial](https://www.law.cornell.edu/wex/trial)

  2. **Procedures to draft complaint, summons, CMP, plaintiff’s discovery to Defendant and Initial defendant’s deposition request.**

1.2.1-Drafting Complaint and Summons:

- Step 1:

On client’s home page on Casepeer, proceed to quickly view the coverages, liability and coverage status to get familiar with the case by looking under defense and plaintiff insurance.

- Step 2:

Proceed to review the case in Sharepoint, starting with the review of Police Report and then with defense and plaintiff Declaration Pages, making sure to have Statement of Coverage, Declaration pages and UM selection/rejection (from pltf Ins.). (Please refer to training video ‘’Personal Injury Case Explanation related to Litigation’ located at: documents/clients/Templates-Ana/Training/6. Litigation, to ensure proper review of the documents). If all docs on file, proceed with step 3 but If any of these is missing, proceed to task accordingly to appropriate staff member to obtain same, (Please refer to Staff Role description sheet located at SP/Clients/Templates-Ana/Training) document your task and move task due date for 1 week and so forth until documents on file. Then proceed with step 3.

- Step 3:

During review of the Police report and Def and Pltf dec pages, you must establish and confirm liability and all defendants that should be named in the complaint and determine which Complaint is needed. (Please refer to ‘’Types of Complaints based on case’s need’’ sheet attached to this procedure to ensure correct one is selected). **Note:** if one of the defendants is a business or commercial entity, please refer to ‘’Procedure how to search businesses or commercial entities on Sunbiz’’ located on SP/Documents/Clients/Clients/AA-Litigation Training Guide.

**Note:** when naming a company/corporation/limited liability company, you must identify if is a foreign/non-profit/for profit and the type of company it is and name it as same in the complaint (I.e. Progressive American Insurance of Illinois, a foreign profit corporation; I.e. Florida Superior Imaging, Inc., a Florida profit corporation.)

- Step 4:

On client’s file home page from Casepeer, proceed to click on ‘’Defense Insurance tab/Adjuster/click on envelope icon/select desired type of complaint. This action will cause the desired complaint to be downloaded.

- Step 5:

Proceed to draft the complaint by adding all necessary information paying attention to all highlighted yellow areas, based on previous review and after complaint is drafted and verified (ensuring no mistakes made), proceed to re-name drafted complaint as follow: Complaint_Client’s name and save word version on client’s/Litigation/Complaint and Summons/Drafts. **Note:** to add the Judicial Circuit Court number to the header in the complaint, proceed to do a google search based on the county were accident happened (I.e. judicial circuit number for Palm Beach County).

- Step 6:

To draft the summons, on client’s file home page from Casepeer, proceed to click on ‘’Defense Insurance tab/Adjuster/click on envelope icon/select desired type of summons. **Note:** If the accident happened in Palm Beach County, the summons template to use will be ‘’Summons – Palm Beach County’’. For the rest of incidents, please use ‘’Summons – General’. This action will cause the desired summons to be downloaded. **Note:** If the summons you are drafting is for a company as the defendant, you will need to add address for the registered agent found during your search on Sunbiz, however, you will not add the actual name of the registered agent and instead, you will just indicate the pleadings are directed to whoever registered agent is.

(i.e. JHON DOE COMPANY, LLC

C/O OR REGISTERED AGENT

Registered Agent address)

**Note:** Please ensure the header on summons and pltf and dft information matches the complaint.

**Note:** If the lawsuit is being filed in Orange/Osceola County, along with the summons, you will need to include ‘’Standing Order’’ (a brief overview of case management plan) which can also be downloaded from Casepeer same way you download the Complaints and Summons. Make sure to select desired one based on county and save it on client’s file/litigation/Complaint and summons/Drafts.

- Step 7:

Proceed to save word version of summons along with Standing order (if applicable) on client’s file/litigation/Complaint and Summons/Filed complaint and summons/Drafts and name summons as follow: Summons_Defendant’s name. (repeat the same process for all defendant's when applicable)

- Drafting Case Management Plan (CMP)

- Step 1:

To draft proposed CMP, proceed to search on google to see if the specific judicial court has their own CMP you should use. To search, you can add: ‘’civil case management plan for xxx county’’. Once you find it, proceed to download same.

- Step 2:

Proceed to calculate all deadlines by going to client’s case on CP/litigation tab on left column and clicking on ‘’Date Calculator’. On next window, proceed to calculate all deadlines accordingly following the prompt and start filling out all calculated deadlines CMP, save on client’s file/litigation/Case Management Plan & Order/CMP_Client’s name and proceed to file it along with summons and plaintiff Discovery to Def.

- Step 2:

After CMP is filed, proceed to calendar all deadlines Casepeer Calendar by going to client’s case on CP, clicking on litigation tab found on left column from home page and adding new event, select deadline, add deadline description on description portion (i.e. Def. John Doe Answer to Complaint), add deadline date and workers assigned to the case (in this case it should be paralegal and paralegal assistant) and click save. Proceed the same way with rest of calculated deadlines.

**Note:** As deadlines are passing, you need to go to particular event on case and mark same as completed so it goes away from calendar.

- Drafting Initial Plaintiff Discovery to Defendant:

- **Step 1:**

To draft initial pltf (Plaintiff) discovery to def. (Defendant), from client’s home page on CP, proceed to click on Defense Insurance/Adjuster/Envelope/Click on desired Plaintiff disco for Def. Based on below description. Proceed to download, fill in all case information (ensure header, pltf and det. Info matches complaint) save on client’s file/litigation/Discovery/Plaintiff request (ensure to rename the word version adding def. Name. I.e. Initial plft disco to def_John Doe). The following are the initial plaintiff disco to defendant along with their initials:

- Request for Admission to Defendant (RFA)

- Request for Production to Defendant (RFP)

- Notice of Interrogatories to Defendant (Rogs)

**Note:** you will select Plaintiff Disco to Deft. Depending on the type of case you are handling. They are as follow:

- For slip and fall and premises liability cases:

Initial RFA to Def – Special

Initial Roggs to Def - Special

Initial RFP to Def – Special

- For driver/owner cases (Auto Accidents):

Initial RFA to Def – Standard

Initial Roggs to Def – Standard

Initial RFP to Def – Standard

- For UM Carrier cases:

Initial RFA to Def – UM

Initial Roggs to Def – UM

Initial RFP to Def – UM

- Mixed cases (I.e. Driver/owner (Company)/UM Carrier)

You might need to propound a combination of Special, Standard and UM carrier disco to def. depending on the situation of the case.

**Note:** plaintiff disco to def must be done per number of defendants and plaintiffs (I.e. if there are 3 defendants and 3 plaintiffs named in the complaint, you will need to propound 6 separate plaintiff disco to def.).

- Drafting initial Plaintiff’s Deposition request of Defendant

From Casepeer, clients home page/Defense Ins./Adjuster/Envelope Icon/Select Initial Defendant’s Deposition request. Save to client’s file/litigation/Deposition/Defendant and name word version as: Initial Defendant’s deposition request_Def. Name.

**Note:** We will NOT file this initial request with complaint,CMP, summons and plaintiff disco to defendant, BUT we will include it with rest of issued pleadings (filed complaint, issued summons and plaintiff disco to defendant).

- Pre-drafting of all litigation documents for the lawsuit

In efforts to be proactive on the proper handling of the new lawsuit and as part of the firm strategy to be proactive, the following are some of the documents we need to have ready and on standby to be filed when time comes and based on the litigation phase case might be in, they are as follow:

- Motion for Clerk’s Default

- Motion for Judicial’s Default

- Motion to Compel Defendant’s Discovery Responses

- Motion to Deem RFA

- Motion to compel better responses

- Plaintiff’s Reply to Defendants affirmative defenses

- Notice of Service of Answers to Defendants Discovery

- Notice of Trial

- Pre-trial Catalogue (Witness, Expert Witness and Exhibit lists)

- Proposal for Settlement (PFS)

- Notice of PFS

**Note:** all these documents can be found on Casepeer/Defense Ins/Adjuster/envelope icon under each one of above names. Save them accordingly on client’s file on SP.

### 1.3 – Procedure to e-file new lawsuit

- Step 1:

Proceed to email drafted complaint, summons, plaintiff disco to def and initial Plaintiff deposition request of def along with PR and pltf and def dec pages to litigation attorney or litigation consultant for review and approval (please CC litigation@[firm domain] and on subject line, please add the client’s name and DOL along with brief message for content of email. (i.e. Case, Test - DOL 05/04/2022 – New complaint, summons, pltf disco to def and initial Plaintiff deposition request of def for review and approval).

- Step 2:

Proceed to document your task on casepeer and move task due date for 1 week to follow up on approval. If not approved by your task due date, proceed to forward initial email (the one containing drafted pleadings) to litigation attorney, making sure to add on subject line the amount of follow up being made (i.e. Case, Test - DOL 05/04/2022 – New complaint, summons, pltf disco to dft and initial Plaintiff deposition request of def for review and approval – 1st follow up and so on. **Note:** Ensure to do same process for all future follow ups so management can see the whole email thread). Document your task accordingly and move the task due date every 3 days until approval is obtained. **Note:** If no approval obtained after 3rd follow up, on next follow up, proceed with previous steps and at this time, CC amontandon@[firm domain] and andrew@[firm domain].

- Step 3:

Once the complaint, summons, plaintiff disco to def and initial Plaintiff deposition request of def is approved, proceed with the e-filling of the complaint ONLY (refer to ‘’How to e-file new lawsuits and pleadings located at SP/Clients/Clients/AA-Litigation training guide/Written procedures). Download filed complaint and save on client’s file/litigation/complaint and summons/filed complaint and summons and re-name document as: Filed complaint_Client’s name.

- Step 4:

Proceed to add all defendants on CP by clicking on defendant’s tab/New Defendant/First and Last name (if a person) or Company Entity (for Commercial def.). After adding all defendants, proceed to add case style (name of the lawsuit) and court name by clicking on litigation tab/Court details and follow the prompt. **Note:** before adding court name, ensure you first check to see if it is already added so you don’t create duplicates. Proceed to document your task, making sure to add previously calculated deadline to serve defendant next to the first line of task (I.e. Please file suit – **DEADLINE TO SERVE DEF: 12/31/23**) and move the task due date for 3 days to follow up on Case number to add to rest of pleadings pending to be filed.

- Step 5:

After filing the complaint, it will generate an email notification sent to litigation@[firm domain] containing the notice of new filing and the filling fees paid. Proceed to save same on client’s file/litigation/Litigation paid Invoices/Filling fees and summons/rename doc to Filling fees_Complaint.

Proceed to add filling fee cost on client’s case on CP by clicking on Cost tab located on left column of case, clicking add cost/select courts/next/select court name/add paid amount/Filed Complaint as Name of Invoice/Memo note and click save. Lastly, from workers tab on home page of file, proceed to assign your name under litigation assistant and then proceed to change status of case on Casepeer from Pending Litigation to Litigation initiated.

- Step 6:

On the task due date, proceed to add Case number to rest of pleadings and proceed to file them. Proceed to download all filed pleadings and save them in client’s file/ litigation/filed Complaint and summons (for the filed complaint and summons only), litigation/Discovery/Plaintiff request (for filed disco to Def) and litigation/Deposition/Plaintiff (for deposition request only). Also, proceed to save the notice of filling containing paid fees and save them in same location as the one for complaint following same process but renaming is as: Filling fees_summons and disco to def. Proceed to add cost to CP following same instructions as described on step 5 but in this case under Invoice you add Filed summons. Document your task and move the task due date for another 3 days to follow up on the issued summons until they have been issued. Once issued summons available, go to 2- Procedure: Servicing pleadings.

**Note:** for some court county, they might issue a Case Management Plan as soon as a complaint is filed if a CMP was not filed initially. In this case, you will need to calendar deadlines in CP calendar.

**Types of Complaints based on case’s need.**

The common information a complaint has which only varies depending on the number of defendants and number of clients suing defendant (if firm represents multiple clients and all claims are pending to be resolved) is the ‘’Common allegations’’ and de number of counts (Counts = number of types of allegations plaintiff makes, i.e., count for negligence, count for vicarious liability, etc.).

- Complaint – Single plaintiff and single defendant

Used when at fault vehicle owner and tortfeasor is same owner and driver of the vehicle, and we represent only one client and there is no UM.

- Complaint – UM

Used when there is only UM coverage available.

- Complaint – UM Phantom Vehicle

Used when there has been a hit and run case and client had UM on the policy.

- Complaint – Multiple Plaintiffs

Used filling lawsuit for multiple clients.

- Complaint – Multiple plaintiffs (Minors)

Used when multiple clients and some of them are minors.

- Complaint – Driver/Owner

Used for cases where the driver of vehicle is one person and driver is somebody else.

- Complaint – Slip and fall/Premises Liability.

Used for premises liability cases and slip and fall cases.

title: Litigation Procedure 2: Service of Pleadings
summary: This is the next step which means plaintiff is attempting to serve defendants and once served, plaintiff waits for filed Notice of Appearance, Answer to Complaint and Affirmative defenses and responses to plaintiff di…
body:
### 2- Service of Pleadings

This is the next step which means plaintiff is attempting to serve defendants and once served, plaintiff waits for filed Notice of Appearance, Answer to Complaint and Affirmative defenses and responses to plaintiff disco to defendant done by defense counsel after defendant have been served. **COURT DEADLINE:** Defendant has **45 calendar days** to answer plaintiff’s complaint (if complaint was served with plaintiff’s disco to def) and **20 calendar days** (if only complaint was served) from the date service was effectuated. Follow steps below to properly process service of pleadings and to ensure correct monitoring of deadlines:

### ( For paralegals from Step 1-5)

- Step 1:urt details/add case number and save. **COURT DEADLINE:** Plaintiff has 120 days to serve the Defendant’s from the date the Complaint is filed.

- Step 2:

Once issued summons received, proceed to send all filed pleadings (filed complaint, plaintiff disco to OC, defendant’s deposition request and issued summons) to process server (we use Ody’s Professional Service) via email to: [[process server email]](mailto:[process server email]) (CC litigation@[firm domain]), making sure to add on subject line, case info and brief content description (i.e. Case, Test - DOL 05/04/2022 – Pleadings to be served on defendant). **Note:** If UM carrier named as defendant, proceed to email pleadings to paralegal supervisor (and not process server) so they can be served through LOSP portal.

- Step 3:

After sending pleadings to the process server, proceed to change status on casepeer from Litigation initiated to Service and proceed to assign task to assistant as follow: Please follow up on ROS (Return of Service) from Ody Professional Service – **DEADLINE to serve: xxx days,** document assistant’s task when pleadings were sent to process server (and if UM carrier named as defendant, document on task when pleadings sent to paralegal supervisor to serve through LOSP) and list all defendants named in the lawsuit and set task due date for next date. Proceed to document your task and move the task due date for 3 weeks to follow up on returned of service (ROS) for all defendants until received and filed with the court system.

- Step 4:

Proceed to add case to master list located at SP/Documents/Clients/Clients/AA-Assignment of Cases/Paralegals/Litigation Cases – By Paralegal, making sure to update all columns as case progresses.

### - Step 5:

If ROS for just one of the defendants received, ensure same was filed with the court system and if not, proceed to e-file it, making sure to download e-filed ROS and save on client’s/litigation/Complaint and summons/Returned of Service and re-name as: filed ROS_Def name. Proceed calculate (if deadline not calculated previously during the CMP drafting) answer to complaint deadline on CP/Litigation tab/Date Calculator and open new task as follow: Follow up on Def. XXX answer to complaint, plaintiff disco responses and def depo dates – **ANSWER TO COMPLAINT DEADLINE: XXXX.** Document the task and move the task due date for same day of deadline to follow up on answer, responses and depo dates from def.

**Note:** for lawsuits filed without the Plaintiff’s disco to def and plaintiff depo request, proceed to move previous task due date for 17-day mark instead of the 20-day mark. On the task due date to check court docket and look for any Notice of Appearance without answer to complaint. Proceed to 2- Procedure: Pending Response for further instructions.

**Note:** If the Defendant cannot be found, you will need to file a motion for extension of time (if first time asking for extension) or motion to serve secretary of state. Please move to the Pending response stage for further instructions regarding this.

### (For paralegal assistants from step 6-7)

- Step 6:

On your task due date, proceed to follow up with process server to obtain confirmation of pleadings have been received by then (do the same with paralegal supervisor if there was UM carrier named as defendant and pleadings sent to file through LOSP). If no answer within a day, continue to move your task due date within 1 day until response received keeping track of deadline to serve all defendants (if after 3rd follow up still no response, inform paralegal supervisor via email (CC litigation@[firm domain]) immediately and wait for further instructions). After confirmation from process server of pleadings received, document your task accordingly and move task due date for 2 weeks to follow up on ROS. **IMPORTANT NOTE:** If confirmation of UM pleadings received from paralegal supervisor, move your task due date for 1 week instead to follow up on ROS until ROS received. Once received, proceed to e-file it and save filed ROS on client’s file same way as described on step 5. (Insurance companies get served within a day and we MUST file ROS with the court as soon as we get it)

- Step 5:

On your task due date, proceed to check on Sharepoint to see if ROS received and if not, proceed to check the docket to see if one was filed but maybe not saved on client’s file and if so, proceed to download and save to client’s file/Litigation/Complaint and Summons/Returned of Service and re-name ROS as: Filed ROS_Def name. If no ROS yet, proceed to document your task accordingly and move the task due date for another 2 weeks to follow up (this may be subject to change depending on deadline for service).

- Step 6:

If on your next task due date there still no ROS filed, for one or more of the defendants (when there is multiple ones) proceed to request from process server via email (using same email thread from initial request) Affidavit of Diligent Search & Concealment (move task due date for 1 day to follow up until it has been received) and email paralegal supervisor (CC litigation@[firm domain]) immediately and ask for further instructions. Move your task due date for 2 days to follow up for those instructions. **Note:** If the process server cannot locate a Defendant, you need to request an Affidavit of Diligent Search & Concealment so that we can serve via the Secretary of State if needed. If we need to serve via secretary of state, please **refer to procedure: Servicing pleadings to Def. Via Secretary of State** located on SP/Document/Clients/Clients/AA - Litigation Training Guide/written procedures.

- Step 7:

If ROS for all defendants received, ensure all of them have been saved on Sharepoint and save all process server invoices (they always reply by email once service has been completed with ROS and invoice) on client’s file/litigation/litigation paid invoices/Process Server/rename each invoice as follow: Service Invoice_$xxx_Def. Xxx (I.e. Service Invoice_$60_Def. John Doe). Proceed to add cost on client’s case on CP/Cost/Process Services/fill in all required tabs/Name under Invoice is Service/Memo: add def. Name. Document your task and move task due date for a day after Answer to complaint is due depending on date first defendant was served (when multiple defendants named in complaint). Proceed to next procedure: Pending Response, for further instructions.

title: Litigation Procedure 3: Pending Response
summary: This is the next step which means plaintiff waits for filed Answer to Complaint and Affirmative defenses, responses to plaintiff disco to defendant done by defense counsel after defendant have been served. COURT DEADL…
body:
### Pending response

This is the next step which means plaintiff waits for filed Answer to Complaint and Affirmative defenses, responses to plaintiff disco to defendant done by defense counsel after defendant have been served. **COURT DEADLINE:** Defendants have only 45 calendar days from the time service was done **if** complaint, stamped summons, plaintiff discovery to defendant and deposition request all served at the same time. Only 20 calendar days to respond **if** only filed complaint and stamped summons served. Proceed with the following steps to ensure proper monitoring of deadlines and follow up on response: ￼

### (For paralegal’s assistants)

- Step 1:

Once ROS received, proceed to calculate answer to complaint due date on CP and add it at the top of your task in bold. Once you have determined the deadline for answer to complaint, proceed to move your task due date for 17-day mark so you can check the docket and look for any Notice of Appearance filed by any potential OC. If notice of appearance filed but no answer to complaint filed within the 17-day mark, proceed to immediately file plaintiff’s disco to OC along with notice of plaintiff depositions request for defendant, document your task accordingly and move task due date for deadline to answer complaint.

- Step 2:

On your task due date, proceed to check client’s file on sharepoint to see if Answer to complaint has been saved and if not, proceed to check court docket to look for same. If answer filed and not saved, proceed to download, and save on client’s file/litigation/Complaint and summons/Answer to affirmative defenses and reply. **Note:** Defense counsel may ask for an extension to answer complaints. Before moving on to the next step if the answer is now overdue, please ensure the defense counsel has not filed any motion for extension of time to answer and if so, check to see if same was granted and for how many more days (we only grant 10 days to answer our complaint). Document your task accordingly and move the task due date for a day after deadline. If otherwise, please move to the next step.

- Step 3:

If defendant did file the answer, proceed to download, and save on client’s file/litigation/complaint and summons/Answer to affirmative defenses and reply/Answer and proceed to draft Reply to Affirmative defenses (if not pre-drafted by paralegal). On casepeer, proceed to click on Defense Ins. tab from client’s home page/adjuster tab envelope icon/and select the following templates to download:

- Reply to Affirmative Defenses
- Designation of email address
- Contention interrogatories

Fill in current case information on highlighted areas, once done, confirm no mistakes done and then proceed to save word version to client’s file/litigation/Complaint and summons/Answer to affirmative defenses and reply/Reply. Proceed to get it approved by paralegal assigned to case by sending it via email (CC litigation@[firm domain]) and follow up on approval every two days and after approval, proceed to e-file it with court system. Document your task or complete it with a note (when applicable, i.e. if all defendants filed answer, etc.)

- Step 4:

Proceed open new task as follows: Def. Disco received (if it is the case) -DEADLINE: add deadline to answer to def disco (I.e. Def. Disco received – **DEADLINE: December 28, 2023).** Proceed to calendar deadline to respond to Def disco on CP and move to **Procedure: Litigation Discovery** for further instructions. Update case on master list.

3.1- **How to handle cases in which an Answer was not filed within deadline by OC**

### ( For Paralegals only)

If an answer to our complaint and responses to our discovery are not filed, we will proceed with the filing of a motion for default. There are two types for motions for default and they can only be filed ONLY when they meet the following criteria:

- Motion for Clerk’s default: used when defendant has not filed anything at all (I.e. Answer to complaint and Affirmative defenses, notice of appearance, any types of motions, etc.). **Note:** for this motion, the court is the one that will grant default and not a judge, therefore, it is not necessary to set it for hearing.

- Motion for Judicial Default: used when defendant might have filed notice of appearance but has failed to file the actual Answer to complaint and affirmative defenses. **Note:** these types of motions are granted by a judge only and they must be set for hearing.

Follow steps below whenever a Motion for Default is needed:

- Step 1:

On your task due date, proceed to check the docket to see if defendant filed their answer and if no answer filed but instead, you see any type of motion filed, proceed to save same on client’s file/litigation/Motions/Defendant. Then proceed to email motion to paralegal supervisor to ask for further instructions. Document your task and move the task due date for 2 days to follow up on response until instructions obtained. If no motions are filed, but criteria already explained above met, proceed with next step. Note: if the motion filed was a Motion to Dismiss, you will need to review the complaint filed and check to see why OC is trying to ask for case to be dismissed as the complaint might need to be amended. Please refer to **procedure: How to amend complaints and how to file amended complaints.**

- Step 2:

Depending on the type of motion for default needed, proceed on casepeer/Defense tab/Adjuster envelope icon/Desired motion for default and download same. This action will cause the template to download. Proceed to fill out with current case information on highlighted yellow areas, verify no mistakes made and then save word version on client’s file/litigation/Motions/Plaintiff.

- Step 3:

Double check in the docket to ensure defendant still did not filed their answer and if no, proceed to file drafted motion for default and set it for hearing (if applicable). Proceed to download filed Motion and save it on client’s file/litigation/Motion/Plaintiff and name it Filed_Motion for xxx Default. Please refer to **procedure: Setting motions for hearing** located on SP/documents/Clients/Clients/AA- Litigation training guide. Document your task and move your task due date for 1 week to follow up on issued default. **Note:** If drafting motion for clerk’s default, you might need an Affidavit of Military Service. - Please email paralegal supervisor for further instructions before filling Motion for Clerk’s Default.

- Step 4:

On your task due date, once issued default is issued, proceed to download same and save it on client’s file (same way previously described) and proceed to email/fax filed motion for default to Ins. adjuster on file and save confirmation of that in client’s file, same location described before (create new folder and name it Fax-email Conf.). Proceed to complete your task with a note (when applicable). Document case on master list. Ask Payton what is next to put in this procedure

title: Litigation Procedure 4: Litigation Discovery
summary: This is the phase of the case in which both sides are gathering their evidence for a potential trial. This is a long and ongoing active phase of the case up until the discovery deadline in which both parties MUST obta…
body:
### 4 – Procedure – Litigation Discovery

This is the phase of the case in which both sides are gathering their evidence for a potential trial. This is a long and ongoing active phase of the case up until the discovery deadline in which both parties MUST obtain all evidence necessary for potential trial before Litigation discovery deadline expires otherwise, when we go to trial (if the case makes it there) the chance of losing the trial is more than 80%. The following events are part of this phase:

- Request for admissions (RFA)
- Request for production (RFP)
- Interrogatories (Roggs)
- Notice of Production Non-party (NPNP)
- Depositions (Def and Pltf)

Part of the firm strategy is to take the driver seat during this phase as soon as possible by propounding our discovery and requesting def. deposition first as this alleviates the pressure of deadlines compliance and more likely we can push he case to be resolved quicker, however, this strategy was implemented only after majority of litigation cases were already in litigation, this means, strategy implemented on or about October/2023.

The following instructions must be followed when handling litigation discovery.

  1. **Defendant’s Discovery to Plaintiff**

Please proceed with next steps to process responses always ensuring deadlines compliance:

- **Step 1:**

- Once discovery req. is filed by OC (opposing counsel), proceed to download it, rename all (i.e. RFA/RFP/Roggs), save them on client’s file/litigation/Discovery/Defendant’s Request. Note: In cases where there are multiple Plaintiff’s, you will create a folder for each Plaintiff inside “Defendant’s Request” and “Plaintiff’s Response”.

- On CP, proceed to create event on client’s case home page by going to litigation tab on left column/New event/Discovery cutoff/add description as: Def. (name of def.) disco to plaintiff/on date – set deadline to file answers/add paralegal and assistant assigned to case and click save. **DEADLINE:** there are only 30 calendar days to file notice of answer to def. discovery (from sending disco to client to respond, prepare responses, send responses to OC and file notice of answers, etc.)

- **Step 2:**
- Proceed to assign the following task to paralegal assistant: Def (name of def.) disco to plaintiff received, please work on disco – **DEADLINE: (Date of deadline to answer to def. disco**. i.e., **DEADLINE: December 30th, 2023**)
- Document task with date def. disco req. was filed and everything they filed (i.e., RFA, RFP, Roggs, NPNP, etc.) set task due date for very next day. If NPNP was filed as well, please go to step 3.

- **Step 3:**
- If NPNP was filed, proceed to assign a separate task for assistant as follow: (Date of filed NPNP) – NPNP Filed – Please draft and file Request for copies and follow up on copies. Set task due date for very next day. **Note:** There might be different NPNPs filed throughout the discovery stage of case, make sure to assign separate tasks EVERYTIME there is a new NPNP filed and repeat same process on this step.
- (For assistant) on task due date, proceed to draft your request for copies and Objection to NPNP (where applicable) which can be found on CP/Defense Ins. tab/Adjuster/envelope/Plaintiff’s Request for Copies/Objection to NPNP. Proceed to download, fill in all case information on highlighted yellow areas, review, save copy on client’s file/litigation/NPNP & RFC/Rename doc as ‘’RFC (date NPNP was filed).
- Email drafted pleadings along with the filed Def. NPNP to litigation consultant specialists for approval and on subject line make sure to add: Client’s name and DOL – Plaintiff req. for copies.
- Document your task with everything done and move the task due date for 2 days until approval obtained. Once approved, proceed to file your request and any applicable objections, save a copy of the filed objection and request in client’s file in previous location and make sure to rename it to RFC (date of NPNP) - Filed.
- After 30 days, proceed to request copies from OC via email. Document your task and move the due date for 2 weeks to make your first request from OC via email. When sending the email request make sure to add on subject line the following: Case style and Case number and attach your filed request for copies to email (cc litigation email).
- Document your task with everything done and move the due date once a month to follow up on request until copies are obtained.
- When copies are obtained, save them on client’s file/litigation/NPNP&RFC/Document produced in response to RFC (Create folder if there isn't one)

### Step 4:

- From client’s home page on CP, proceed to draft Discovery letter to client by clicking on Client’s tab/Contact detail/Envelope/Discovery letter to client (prefer language), download, fill in any highlighted areas in yellow with case information, review and save on client’s file/litigation/Discovery and name as “Discovery letter to client”
- Proceed to convert RFA to word document and respond same. Review and save on client’s file under “Plaintiffis Response” and name “Plaintiff’s Response to Defendant’s RFA”. **Note:** RFA’s are admit or deny answers. Admissions are always admissible in court, a denial is not.)
- Email filled out RFA to litigation specialists' consultant for approval (direct email to litapproval@[firm domain]), making sure to add in subject line: Client’s name – DOL – Discovery letter and def. xxx disco to client for approval. Follow up on approval until it is received (should not take more than 2 follow ups, if so, consult with paralegal supervisor immediately).

- **Step 5:**
- After filled out RFA is approved, proceed to call client to educate them on what you’ll be sending and what it is and the importance of them answering it in a timely manner (you can read explanation to client from disco letter). Make sure to confirm client’s information during the phone call such as email address, any emergency contact they would like to provide in case we can’t get a hold of them and best mailing address (update client’s information if applicable). Note: we only email interrogatories to the client, not RFA or RFP.
- Once all of the above is done, proceed to email Disco letter to client along with Rogs and on subject line add: Regarding Your Case - Discovery. **Note:** Inform the client in the email that the discovery responses need to be returned to our office within 10 days at the latest & the last page of the interrogatories will need to be notarized. Make sure to save email confirmation on client’s file/litigation/Discovery/To Plaintiff/Confirmation (create folder if needed).
- If the client does not have an email address, proceed to request from reception the Disco letter and Roggs to be mailed out certified mail and provide client’s mailing address. Ensure reception mails the packet the same day by checking in folder ‘’Proof of mailed items’’ and look for proof of mailing of your request. If no proof of mailing in folder, follow up with reception until is done (should not take more than 2 days to be mailed out, if so, inform paralegal supervisor immediately).
- Once disco sent to client, proceed to file your approved RFA, making sure to save a copy of filed RFA to client’s file/litigation/Discovery/to plaintiff/rename as Plaintiff’s Response to Defendant’s RFA - Filed
- Document your task with your progress and move task due date for 2 days to confirm client received email. If the request was mailed, move your task due date for 1 week to follow up with client to ensure they received it by mail.

- **Step 6:**
- On your task due date, check to see if client responded acknowledging your email and if not, proceed to forward same email and ask client to please confirm receipt of same and, at the same time, call client and ask for the email acknowledgement and once again explain client this is a time sensitive matter and needs to be addressed as soon as possible. If no answer, leave VM and send text message to client asking for confirmation of email receipt.
- Move task due day for every 2 days to follow up on acknowledgement but no more than 2 follow ups should be made and if is the case, inform paralegal assigned to case immediately (make sure to follow up procedure to contact unresponsive clients located in SP/Documents/Clients/Templates-Ana/Training/Written procedures) until confirmation received (ensure you are paying attention to deadline to respond to disco).
- Once client has confirmed disco packet was received, proceed to convert discovery request (Rogs and RPF) to word version so you can answer the questions which client’s responses are not needed and to also start preparing all documents needed in response to RFP (Please refer to: Standard Answers to Def. Disco found attached to this procedure at the bottom of same, to guide yourself which questions can be answered without client’s responses and which docs should be included on response to RFP),
- Proceed to document your task and move your task due date every 3 days for follow up with client until responses received. **Note:** If no responses received by the 15-day mark of deadline, inform paralegal assigned to the case via email using same email you sent to obtain approval RFA (following same instructions on every email sent to them) of the situation so further instructions can be provided. Proceed to assign task as follow: Client has not sent answers to def. xxx disco. Please check on next steps.

### For paralegals:

- If the deadline is approaching (15-days away from deadline) and you have been informed by your assistant that we still don’t have client’s responses, proceed to pre-draft MFE to Answer Def. Dico and Agreed Order (AO) on Plaintiff's MFE to Answer Def. discovery located on client’s file on CP/Defense Ins tab/adjuster/envelope/ Agreed Order on Plaintiff's MFE to Answer Def. Discovery and MFE to Answer Def. Disco.
- Review your work and save doc on client’s file/litigation/Discovery/to plaintiff/request for extension of time to OC (create folder if necessary), file MFE to Answer Def. Disco (make sure to save filed copy on client’s file in same location as descried before).
- Proceed to email OC (cc litapproval email) add on subject line: Case style (name of filed lawsuit) – Case No. Xxx and request an extension of 30 additional days to respond and make sure to attach drafted AO. Document your task and set a due date for every 2 days to follow up with their response until response obtained but no more than 2 follow ups should be made.
- If after 2 follow ups, they still don’t respond, just wait until they actually respond to your email. If OC does not agree to the request, proceed to set the motion for hearing (refer to Procedure: Setting motions for hearing).
- If Motion granted, make sure to replace deadline with new one on assistant’s task (at the top). If client still has not sent responses by the time deadline on granted motion is due, then instruct assistant to file them unverified but to continue to follow up on answers until they are received and that once they are received, they need to file the answers as verified.

**Note:** We will only file unverified answers ONLY if we are going to be in violations of an order.

- **Step 7:**
- Once you have received the client’s responses to def. Rogs, proceed to fill in client’s responses on Rogs req., review answers to rogs and if any other additional documents needed and not in our possession, proceed to email client asking for the needed documents using same email you sent containing the disco request.
- After email sent to client, proceed to call client to explain what you need and why, document your task and move task due date for 4 days to follow up with client until docs received (**Note:** if deadline approaching, inform paralegal immediately following instructions provided on step 6).
- Proceed to combine and compress all documents needed for RFP and re-name it as: RFP packet. Review your work to ensure no mistakes are made and save them on client’s file (same location as before. If multiple defendants, create a folder for each defendant and add to name of docs: Plaintiff’s response to Defendant’s Interrogatories
- Proceed to use the same email sent to litigation specialists' consultant when requesting approval of RFA, to send client’s answers and RFP packet for review and approval (cc litapproval@[firm domain]). In the subject line, replace the ‘’Discovery letter and def. xxx disco to client for approval’’ with ‘’Plaintiff’s answers and RFP packet’’ for approval (on body of email make sure to add deadline to respond to disco).
- Document your task with everything done and move the due date every 2 days to follow up on approval (it should not take more than 2 follow ups for docs to be approved, if so, consult with paralegal supervisor immediately).

- **Step 8:**
- After answers and docs approved, proceed to draft Notice of Service of Answers to Def. Rogs by going to client’s case on CP/Defense Ins. tab/adjuster/envelope/select your desired docs from the list.
- Proceed to fill in all case information on highlighted yellow areas, review your work and save docs on client’s file/litigation/discovery/to plaintiff/re-name docs: Notice of Service of Answers to Def. XXX Rogs
- **NOTE 1: DO NOT** file interrogatory responses or request for production package. **ONLY** file the notice of service of interrogatories, request for production response, and response to request for admissions.
- **NOTE 2: DO NOT** file anything containing confidential information (social security numbers, etc.)

- Proceed to send both docs to paralegal assigned to case (cc litigation email) using same previous email for the approval of the answers making sure to replace ‘’Plaintiff’s answers and docs to Def. xxx rogs and RFP’’ for approval – DEADLINE to file answer xxx with ‘’NOS of rogs and RFP for approval.’’
- Document your task and move the due date for 2 days to follow up on approval until it is obtained. **Note:** it should not take more than 2 follow-ups to obtain approval, if so, inform the paralegal supervisor immediately.

- **Step 9:**
- After approval obtained from paralegal, proceed to email OC the actual answers to rogs and docs produced (cc litigation email) and make sure to add on subject line: Case Style and Case number.
- Proceed to save email confirmation on client’s file/litigation/Discovery/to plaintiff/Confirmation (create folder if necessary). After that, proceed to file the notice of answers to interrogatories and response to request for production and make sure to save a copy of the filed notices on client’s file in same location and add to name of docs: Notice of Service of Answers to Def. John Doe Roggs - Filed etc.). Proceed to complete your task with a note of everything done and proceed to mark event on client’s case on CP as completed.
- Proceed to look for deadline when litigation discovery needs to be done by both parties and after that, proceed to assign task to paralegal assigned to case as follow: Please draft plaintiff’s discovery to defendant as soon as possible (add deadline IN BOLD when litigation discover needs to be done by both sides based on CMP), i.e. Please draft plaintiff’s discovery to defendant as soon as possible – **DEADLINE: March 12, 2024).** And set due date for very next day if we have not propounded plaintiff’s discovery to defendant.

  2. **Plaintiff’s Discovery to Defendant**

Since most of the cases currently in litigation were filed without the initial plaintiff’s discovery to defendant propounded, this procedure will be split into 2 parts. The first part will be the steps to follow to draft, propound and follow up on plaintiff’s disco to defendant.

Part two will contain the steps to follow on propounded discovery to defendant.

**4.2.1 – For cases in which Plaintiff’s Discovery to Defendant was not propounded during the filing of the lawsuit.**

Please follow the steps below:

- **Step 1:**
- Proceed to assign the following task to paralegal assigned to case: Please draft plaintiff’s discovery to defendant as soon as possible (add deadline IN BOLD when litigation discover needs to be done by both sides based on CMP), i.e. Please draft plaintiff’s discovery to defendant as soon as possible – **DEADLINE: March 12, 2024).** And set the due date for very next day. **Note:** This will indicate that discovery should be done prior to discovery deadline.
- Proceed to assign task to litigation scheduler as follows: Please coordinate defendant’s deposition as soon as possible (add deadline IN BOLD when litigation discovery needs to be done by both parties) i.e. Please coordinate defendant’s deposition as soon as possible – **DEADLINE for Discovery: March 12, 2024.** And set the task due date for the very next day. **Note:** This will indicate that deposition should be done prior to discovery deadline.

- **Step 2:**

### For paralegals:

- Proceed to properly review the type of case you have in order to determine which type of discovery needs to be drafted and to ensure the correct way of doing it. For this, please refer to 1- Procedure: Initiation of the law suit/ Drafting initial plaintiff’s discovery to defendant.
- Proceed to pre-draft the following motions (for all defendants when multiple ones) and carefully review them as it will be considered approved by you:
- Motion to compel Defendant’s Discovery responses
- Motion to deem RFA
- Motion to compel better answers

For this, please refer again to 1- Procedure: Initiation of the lawsuit/ 1.2/Pre-drafting of all litigation documents for he lawsuit so you know how to properly do it.

- Once you have drafted plaintiff’s disco to defendant, proceed to complete your task with note with everything done.
- Proceed to assign task to paralegal assistant as follows: Please propound Plaintiff’s Discovery to Defendant and follow up on responses – **DEADLINE to respond: xxxx.** Set task due date for next day.
- **Note:** Please check emails carefully in the event OC emails us asking for an extension of time to answer our disco. If so, you can grant them ONLY 10 additional days to answer our disco. Make sure to document your assistant’s task with what you granted to OC and make sure to update DEADLINE in same task as well as update event on client’s case.

- **Step 3:**

### For paralegal assistants

- On your task due date, proceed to save drafted Plaintiff’s discovery to Defendant(s) as a PDF doc and then proceed to compress all of them into one using Adobe Acrobat. Rename all docs as: Pltf Disco to XXX Defendant_Client’s name (repeat same process for all plaintiff and defendants if applicable).
- Proceed to file compress docs and save copy of filed Plaintiff disco to defendant(s) on client’s file/litigation/Discovery/to defendant/add to existing name: Filed (along with rest of name. i.e. Filed Plaintiff’s Disco to xxx def.).
- Proceed to add event on client’s case on CP/Litigation tab on left column/New event/Event type – Discovery/Description – Deadline: Def. xxx answer to disco/date – answer to disco date/add paralegal and assistant assigned to case and click save.
- Proceed to document your task with the progress made, making sure to properly list all defendants for which plaintiff disco was filed (for cases with multiple defendants) and move your task due date for day of deadline for answer to plaintiff’s disco to follow up on responses and produced docs.

- **Step 4:**
- On your task due date, proceed to check court docket to see if any of the defendants have filed their notices of servicing responses, if so, proceed to save same on client’s file in same location described on step 3 and re-named docs as: NOS of answered name client’s name (repeat same process for all plaintiffs and defendant when applicable).
- Proceed to look for the email from OC containing defendants responses and produced docs, proceed to save on client’s file/litigation/Discovery/to defendant/re-name docs depending on what they are (i.e. Answer to rogs_def. xxx_client’s name, etc.) compress all documents provided by OC using adobe acrobat and re-name accordingly. If no NOS filed by def. and no answers and docs received, go to step 7.

- **Step 5:**
- Proceed to email paralegal assigned to case the answers and docs received along with plaintiff disco to defendant to review and to ensure everything looks in order. On subject line of email add: Case name – DOL – Case No – Def. xxx answer to disco – for review and further instructions.
- Assign task to paralegal as follow: Def. xxx answers to plaintiff disco received. Please review.
- Document your task and move the task due date for 2 days to follow up on paralegals instructions.

- **Step 6:**

### For paralegals

- Once you receive the responses and docs to plaintiff disco to defendant, proceed to review answers and docs carefully based on request sent to def. Proceed to forward email sent to you by your assistant to litigation attorney for review and approval of responses to obtain further instructions regarding disco (in the event we need to file motion for better responses, etc.).
- Document your task and move the due date for 2 days to follow up on further instructions from the attorney. If the attorney instructs anything else needs to be done, proceed with documenting your task and your assistant’s task accordingly.

- **Step 7:**
- If any or none of the defendants have not responded to Plaintiff disco to defendant, proceed to check if OC emailed us asking for an extension of time to respond to our disco and if so, paralegal should have responded to them and should have updated new task deadline for assistant so it reflects new deadline, however, if you see no new deadline under your task but you do see OC request, proceed to forward email to paralegal and copy paralegal supervisor aside of litigation email.
- if no email from OC, email OC for the defendant(s) (on subject line add: client’s case name – DOL – Def. xxx answer to discovery – 1st follow up) asking for the answers and documents (cc litigation email).
- Document your task and move date for 2 days to follow up on response from OC.

- **Step 8:**
- On your task due date, if there is still no email from OC, proceed to send a second and final one making sure to add on your subject line – 2nd and final follow up.
- Document your task and move due date for another 2 days.

- **Step 9:**
- On your task due date, if still no response and no answers from OC, at this point use same email thread to email paralegal assigned to case and inform of the situation so the next steps can be taken.
- Proceed to assign task to paralegal as: Please proceed with next steps and provide further instructions.
- Document paralegal’s task with everything going on and set task due date for next day.

### For paralegals:

- Once your assistant outs you on notice that one or more defendants have not answered to our disco, proceed to review you pre-drafted motion to compel and add necessary details (if applicable), review and save on client’s file in previous location where initial one was.
- Proceed to file it and set it for hearing immediately. (Please refer again to: Procedures: Setting motions for hearing). Document your task and move date according to procedure for hearing.
- Document your assistant’s task of the situation but encourage assistant to continue to follow up on responses to disco until received.

- **Step 10:**
- After responses received, please refer to step 5 and follow the instructions. If the instructions are to close your task, proceed to complete with note.

title: Litigation Procedure 5: Scheduling Depositions, Mediation, CME and Conference Calls
summary: 1. Coordinating Depositions: (Depositions start ONLY at 11:00 AM and CAN’T START AFTER 2:00 P.M.)
body:
### Procedures for coordinating Depositions, CME, Mediation and Conference Calls

1. **Coordinating Depositions: (Depositions start ONLY at 11:00 AM and CAN’T START AFTER 2:00 P.M.)**

A [deposition](https://www.law.cornell.edu/wex/deposition) is a sworn out-of-court testimony given by a witness in the presence of a court reporter (person transcribing deposition discussion) requested by defendant’s lawyer. The plaintiff’s lawyer is present and so is the defendant’s lawyer. If plaintiff’s lawyer deems necessary deposing defendant, this will then be requested by plaintiff from defendant’s lawyer. Depositions are part of the discovery process, which is a pretrial investigation into the facts of a case. The discovery phase allows all parties to gather information and evidence that may be used at trial.

Depositions are usually conducted by an attorney for the other side or opposing counsel. The deposition will be recorded, and the plaintiff will be placed under oath. The attorney will ask plaintiff questions about the accident and plaintiff’s injuries which plaintiff should answer these questions truthfully. To coordinate deposition requested from opposing counsel, please proceed with the following steps:

### Coordinating Plaintiff’s Deposition:

- **Step 1:**

When opposing counsel reaches out to coordinate client’s deposition, please confirm with OC if deposition will be via zoom as we only agree to zoom depos, then, proceed to assign task on Casepeer as follow: **Deposition request from Opposing Counsel received, please coordinate deposition** and document your task with said dates (ensure you type full dates, I.e.: 2/24/24, 3/25/24, etc).

- **Step 2:**

When opposing counsel provides available dates, you must verify your attorney's availability by checking his calendar on CP for those dates (CP Calendar starting January 2024. Rest for 2023 year, remains in outlook), making sure the calendar slot is BLANK (NOTHING ELSE ADDED TO IT WITHIN THE REQUESTED TIME FRAME) and does not have any other events on Hold. If the slot is blank, proceed to block it for ONLY 3 HOURS (meaning adding the time for which the slots for the number of hours needed) unless the attorney instructs you differently. To block or add the event on CP calendar, proceed to CP/calendar/click on case from left column and select desired month and date and add the block, case name, paralegal assigned to case and which attorney will be covering the depo and click create. Pic below:

**Step 3:**

Proceed to call the client to inform them their deposition has been scheduled for that date and educate the client **(explain what is a deposition, they have to be presentable, having picture ID, you have to be by yourself and should not be driving, nobody should be in the room with you, they should be on time, they must attend because failure to attend might result in monetary sanctions imposed against your case or potential dismissal of your case, and if they need assistance on using ZOOM, they must inform you at least a day before the deposition to avoid unnecessary delays for all the parties involved)** and to ensure they are available as well. Proceed to ask the client if they will need to have a translator present at the deposition, then proceed with step 4.

- **Step 4:**

Once the date has been confirmed (with attorney and client) proceed to respond to opposing counsel via email (CC litigation@[firm domain]) of date and time and inform them client will need a translator (when applicable and specify which language). **Note:** Opposing counsel will hire and pay for translators and court reporters for depositions ONLY.

- **Step 5:**

Proceed to document your task with all steps taken before and move your task due date for 2 days to get confirmation from OC and after that, move due date for 1 week to follow up on the filed ‘’Notice of Taking Plaintiff’s Deposition’ and zoom link.

- **Step 6:**

On your task due date, proceed to check Sharepoint to see if Notice of taking plaintiff’s deposition has been saved. Via Zoom. Link: xxxxxxxxxxxxxxx – if adding on outlook). On Casepeer, proceed to draft ‘Deposition letter to client’ by downloading template as follow: From client’s home page on Casepeer, click on ‘’Client’’ tab, then on ‘’Envelope’’ icon and select ‘’Depo Letter to client’ from drop down menu. **Note:** Ensure you select client’s prefer language when sending depo letter. You must add missing information to the letter by filling in highlighted lines in yellow. 1. **Coordinating Mediation or Arbitration**

Mediation is a process where each side of a case agrees to use a neutral third party to try to resolve the claim without going to trial.

Civil Rules Procedures indicates at least one Mediation MUST be done prior to trial which MUST be requested by Plaintiff. Once the case is set for mediation, plaintiff’s attorney and the insurance defense attorney will try to agree on who to use as the mediator. The mediator is the neutral third party. Both parties agree on a date, time, location, and mediator. Please follow the steps below when coordinating mediation:

Proceed to assign task as follows: **Please coordinate mediation (if mediation) or Please coordinate Arbitration (if arbitration).** Check the client’s file for a case management plan & order or any other order that may have a deadline for mediation or there is an order for any Arbitration (i.e. order directing us to mediation or arbitration, order setting calendar call, etc.) – Generally, all cases have a deadline which mediation or arbitration must take place by. 2. **Coordinating Compulsory Medical Examination (CME)**

A compulsory medical examination (CME) is an examination conducted by an insurance carrier’s physician that a company uses in an injury lawsuit. Under Florida Rules of Civil Procedure 1.360, a defendant (the insurance company) can ask the plaintiff to undergo a medical examination by the doctor of the defendant’s choice. However, a CME request must be backed up with evidence. The insurance company can ask for a compulsory medical examination (CME) under certain circumstances by claiming that:

- The condition clients are claiming is being disputed.
- It wants proof of an accident victim’s injuries.
- It believes client is lying about or exaggerating the extent of their injury.

As the plaintiff in a personal injury case, our client must undergo a requested CME to prove their injuries are legitimate and not exaggerated. Client must show the injuries require medical care and that they have suffered damage or losses as a result.

Since the insurance company employs the physicians who conduct these examinations and want to minimize client’s injuries and find weaknesses in client’s case, there are objections we file to certain request. The medical examiner must provide a copy of the report to all parties and the examiner can also serve as a witness and be called to testify in court if the case makes it to trial.

It is imperative clients cooperate and attend to CME requested by defendant. Otherwise, the client can face severe consequences including but not limited to court sanctions and the potential dismissal of their cases.

Please follow the steps below when CME is requested by Defendant:

### Step 1:

After receiving CME request or unilaterally set by OC with proposed dates or getting Notice of CME, proceed to assign task to scheduler with the following: **CME Requested by Def.
