body:
### Proposal for Settlement (PFS)

This is a proposal any of the parties might make to try to resolve the case without the need to move the case further to mediation or trial. This is an extremely sensitive matter because If we fail to present it to the client and the case makes it to trial and we obtain a verdict of 25% less than the proposal for settlement, the defendant will be allowed to tax attorney’s fees, cost and expenses against the client,x which could result in catastrophic consequences for the law firm including but not limited to potential malpractice lawsuits. As such, it is IMPERATIVE that all staff members responsible for the proper handling of this matter know how to handle it correctly. For these reasons, please make sure to follow the following steps when presenting PFS to clients as well as when we need to service a PFS on defendants:

**Deadline:** 30 days to respond, which applies to both parties. Please proceed with the following steps to know how to respond to Defendant’s PFS and how to file plaintiff PFS:

### 6.1- Defendant’s PFS to Plaintiff

Please proceed with following steps:

- **Step 1:**

1. (For whoever sees PFS first). As soon as Def. Notice of PFS is filed or received via email from OC, proceed to save it on client’s file/Litigation/PFS/to Plaintiff/rename as: (Date of filed PFS)_Filed Def. xxx PFS_$pfs amount_cient’s name (i.e. (12/1/23)_Filed Def. John Doe PFS_$500_Test Case). **Note:** If more than 1 PFS received and from different defendants, you MUST create defendants name inside of ‘’To Plaintiff’ folder, I.e. Def. - John Doe, Def. Karen Doe, etc.

2. Proceed to assign task to paralegal’s assistant as follow: (Date of PFS filed) – Def. xxx PFS for $amount received – **DEADLINE to respond: January 1, 2024**. (i.e. (12/1/23) – Def. John Dow PFS for $500 received – **DEADLINE to respond: January 1, 2024.** Set task due date for next day.

3. Proceed to create event on client’s case on CP/Litigation tab on left column/New event/Event type – Other/Description – Def. xxx $amount PFS – Response due/Date – PFS response deadline/add paralegal, and assistant assigned to case and click save.

4. Proceed to add PFS offer under case settlement tab on CP located on left column. If demand was never added, you first need to add demand by going under same tab (Settlement)/Settlement proceeds arrow/select what type of demand was sent based on CP information (Defense – third party/Plaintiff – UM Demand)/Defendant Ins – pick desired one/click policy limits option/select date sent (correct way is when demand was sent but it is a new feature we never used so just pick whatever date) and click save.

5. Once demand has added, proceed to edit fee logic (in case fee is not 33 1/3%) by clicking on arrow next to Ins. Company name/Edit fee logic/Percentage: 40% and click save.

6. Proceed to add PFS amount by clicking on arrow next to the insurance company name/select Add offer/Offer date: Add date of filed PFS/under amount: PFS amount/under Note: Def. xxx PFS $amount and click save. **Note:** If the case has multiple plaintiffs, you MUST add event under each separate case as they should be treated separately even though they are in same accident.

- **Step 2:**

1. Proceed to assign lien negotiator to the case by clicking on Workers tab from client’s home page on CP/Lien negotiator/Select desired lien negotiator and click save. Then proceed to assign task (if one is not already assigned) to lien negotiator as follow: PFS for $amount of PFS received, please review file for reductions asap – **DEADLINE to respond to PFS: January 1, 2024 ,** set priority to Urgent, trigger date: On due date and set task due date for next day.

- **Note:** the lien negotiators currently available in the office can be found on our Staff members and role description sheet located in sp/document/clients/1- Pre-Litigation and Litigation Firm Procedures/Staff members and job description.

2. Proceed to assign task to Attorney Associate as follow: PFS (Date filed) for $amount received, please convey to client as soon as possible. Thank you – DEADLINE to respond: Response due date and set task due date for the next two days.

- **Step 3:**

### For Paralegal

1. Proceed to email attorney associate the PFS letter received by OC, making sure to add on subject line: Client’s name – DOL – Def. xxx $amount of PFS to client.

2. Proceed to document your task and move your task due date for 1 week to follow up on instructions from attorney associate after he present the PFS to client (cc litigation email).

3. Document your task and move due date for 2 days to follow up again and so on until instructions received (no more than 3 follows should be made, if after your third follow up you don’t get a response, MAKE SURE to CC paralegal supervisor, office manager and management on that email).

- **Step 4:**

### For Attorney Associate:

1. After you receive an email from paralegal assistant containing PFS to client, proceed to check if reductions estimates are available (if net sheet or settlement information on CP available). If no estimates are available yet, please document your task and move the task due date for 1 week to follow up again.

2. Once reductions estimate available, proceed to call client. If the call attempt is successful, proceed to convey the PFS offer to client making sure to properly explain everything regarding the PFS. While on the phone, confirm client’s contact information such as current mailing address, any emergency contact information client will like to provide, best email address, etc. and then inform client he/she must formally accept or rejecting in writing and that after the phone conversation, we will be sending them PFS letter containing everything that was discussed via docusign so it can be executed and also via certified mail.

3. After conversation with client, proceed to document your task with everything discussed with client, move task due date for another week to make sure PFS letter was sent to client. Update client’s information on CP (if anything changed or needs to be updated) and proceed to respond to email paralegal assistant sent providing the necessary instructions (sending PFS letter to client, etc.)

- **Step 5:**

### For Paralegal:

1. Once instructions received from attorney associate via email (instructions should be client is either rejecting or accepting offer), proceed draft PFS letter to client by going on CP/Client contact/Contact details/Envelope/Desired PFS Letter to client – preferred language.

2. Proceed to request a certified mail tracking no from reception via email, making sure to add on subject line: OUTGOING MAIL REQUEST – Client’s name – DOL – PFS for mailing Certified mail (cc litigation email). Make sure to obtain tracking no. same day.

3. Fill in all case information in highlighted yellow areas, add tracking no provided by reception, review your work and save word version on client’s file/litigation/PFS/to plaintiff/re-name file as: (date pfs was filed)_PFS Letter to Client_Client’s name, i.e. (12/1/23)_PFS Letter to Client_Client’s name.

- **Step 6:**

1. Proceed to email drafted PFS along with PFS letter to client to paralegal assigned to case for approval (cc litigation email) making sure you add on subject line: Client’s name – DOL – (12/1/23)_PFS Letter to Client_Client’s name – for approval.

2. Proceed to document your task and move task due date for 2 days and so on until approval received from paralegal (there should not be more than 2 follow ups, if so, email paralegal supervisor immediately)

- **Step 7:**

1. Once PFS letter to client has been approved, proceed to send approved PFS letter (make sure to save to PDF) to client’s regular email and also via docusign so client can sign electronically and send client a CP text message letting hleim/her know you already sent the document and he/she needs to sign it. Make sure to save email sent to client onto client’s file in previous location and in it, create folder as Confirmation.

2. Proceed to email PFS letter to reception using exact same email initially sent when you requested the certified tracking no. so letter can also be mailed out.

3. Document your task and move the due date to the next day to ensure the letter was mailed out to the client. Next day, check client’s folder on SP/Proof of mailed items/Litigation to see if proof of mailing was uploaded. If not, follow up with reception immediately and make sure it gets mailed out the same day. If the letter is mailed out, document your task and move due date for 2 days.

- **Step 8:**

1. On your task due date, proceed to check docusign to see if client signed the letter. If so, proceed to download from docusign and save it on client’s file/litigation/PFS and rename document making sure to add either Accepted or rejected to rest of name.

2. If the client did not sign the letter via docusing, proceed to track the letter by going to usps.com and add tracking no. on the website and see if it shows delivered. Regardless if it was delivered or not, proceed to call client to follow up on receipt of letter and execution of same (making sure to follow Procedure: How to contact unresponsive clients if client does not answer).

3. If client ack. Letter was received, proceed to encourage client to execute the letter sent via docusign and also to send back signed mailed PFS.

4. Document your task accordingly and move task due date for 2 days and on until signed PFS received or until expiration (if applicable).

- **Step 9:**

1. Once signed response received, proceed to save same on client’s file/litigation/PFS/Re-name it: (Date of filed PFS)_Client’s acceptance or rejection (whichever applies) xxx PFS.

2. Proceed to mark event as complete of client’s case on CP and set task to paralegal supervisor as follow: Client accepted PFS, please review file for potential filling of Notice of Settlement.

3. If the client accepts PFS, proceed to draft Notice of Acceptance of PFS by going on CP/Defense Ins tab/Adjuster/Notice of Acceptance and re-name same by just adding ‘’Date PFS was filed PFS, to existing name (I.e. Notice of Acceptance of PFS_Test Case_12.7.23 - PFS and save on client’s file on designated folder described before.

4. Proceed to send drafted Notice of PFS along with the Def. PFS (containing def name, to which plaintiff and amount) to paralegal assigned to case for approval via email (CC litapprovals@[firm domain]). Document task and set due date for 2 days to follow up on approval until obtained (make sure to monitor deadline to respond)

5. Once Notice approved, proceed to file it, save filed copy on client’s file, document task for lien negotiator already assigned and complete your task with notes.

### For attorney Associate:

1. If PFS was accepted by client, proceed to check and confirm if case is now 100% settled by checking case coverages on SP (police report, dec pages, any excess, umbrella policies, etc.)

2. Regardless of if case is settled 100% or not, proceed to update settlement offer on CP, either to rejected or accepted depending on the situation, go to settlement tab/locate the desired offer you would like to update/click on arrow next to amount/edit offer details (if client is rejecting)/Note: (Date of filed pfs) PFS amount rejected. If a client accepting offer, click on Accept offer from drop down list display after clicking arrow next to offer amount/select Money pending and click save.

title: How to Request and Obtain Medical Records and Bills
summary: When our clients are actively treating, we need to start gathering medical reports to start properly documenting the client’s injuries and therefore, to start properly building our client’s cases. This also applies wh…
body:
### Procedure – How to request and obtain medical records and bills.

When our clients are actively treating, we need to start gathering medical reports to start properly documenting the client’s injuries and therefore, to start properly building our client’s cases. This also applies when the case is ready to go in demand and we need to collect all missing records and bills.

During this stage of the case, the Firm covers all the costs associated with these requests, including but not limited to record/bills request invoices which we often first need to cover before the requested documents can be released to us. Due to the associated cost of all cases, we must pay close attention to the status of the case, more importantly, in the event the Firm has decided to withdraw representation for any reasons from a case, which in this case, all request and work should be stopped immediately. Example of such status including but not limited to the following:

- Drop review.
- Pending drop

1. **To submit initial request for medical records and bills**

After retaining the case and client starts treating, we must send the initial request to treating providers for the first time along with our medical letter of representation. Follow below steps to proceed with same:

- Step 1:
1. Proceed to add provider on CP (if provider not added already) clicking on Health

providers/new provider.

On the next screen, type providers name on search tab to see if that provider is already in our database (this will ensure we don’t create duplicated providers).

**Note:** if providers name is showing up multiple times, proceed to select the one with the most clients added to it.

Proceed to update treatment status (if applicable) and click save.

2. If medical provider was never added in our database, proceed to google medical facility online to find their phone number, call them and ask them the following:
- Correct name of their facility and confirmation of their address
- Best way to request medical records and bills.
- Best way to send reductions request and follow ups.
1. Proceed to add a new provider in our database after obtaining all information by following previous steps until you see the name of provider does not come up in the search. After that, proceed to click on Add provider and fill in all information previously obtained. Note: All information can also be added under section ‘’Note’’ and then click save at bottom of page.

After successfully adding provider, please proceed to the next step.

- Step 2:

1. Proceed to extract in PDF signed HIPAA authorization which can be found in executed retainer on client’s file/Intake/retainer in Sharepoint and rename it as HIPAA_ and save it on client’s medical folder/1. Medical LOR & HIPPA for future use as you will be using it to request other medical records and bills as the case progresses. Refer to picture below for HIPAA form.

2. Proceed to prepare the signed HIPAA authorization by downloading from SP the HIPAA form previously saved (please don’t work on top of the form you just saved as that should be the template for future use) and insert medical facility’s name to HIPAA form, rename it as HIPAA_Medical facility (i.e. HIPAA_Spine and Brain Surgery). Save it on client’s file in same previous location.

- Step 3:

1. After preparing HIPAA authorization and saving it on client’s file, proceed to download Medical LOR template by going on client’s case on CasePeer/Health providers tab/Provider’s name/Envelope icon/Medical rep letter.
- **Note:** for EMS and ER request through CIOX, you will download Hitech – Medical records CIOX template instead. For any other EMS and ER NOT through CIOX, you will download HITECH Medical Records & Bills request instead.

2. Proceed to click on the desired template and modify letter as needed (ex. Adding source you are sending it, etc) and click ‘’save as’’ and rename letter by adding medical facility name at end of initial name (Medical Rep Letter_Client’s name_Medical facility name).
3. After step 3 is completed, proceed to upload medical rep letter (word and PDF version) on client’s file, same location as you previously saved prepared HIPPA described on previous steps.

- Step 4:

1. Once all steps from 1-3 are completed, proceed to submit your request. If your request is being sent via fax or email, please add the following on subject line: Attn: Records/billing department (whichever applies) – Records and bills request (which ever applies) – Client’s name and DOL (Ex. Attn: Billing dept. – Reduction request - Case, Test - DOL 05/04/2022). If sending via fax, also ensure to use font size 28.
2. On the body of your email/fax, make sure you provide the information you need and ask them to send you the requested records and bills to records@[firm domain] ONLY.
3. It is IMPERATIVE you save fax/email confirmation of your request on client’s file/Medical/1. Medical LOR & HIPAA/Fax-email Conf. and re-name your request based on type of request and which provider (Ex. Pagano Chiropractic_initial report req_Conf..; Spine and Brain surgery_recs and bills req. Conf, etc.).
- **Note:** for the fax confirmation, you must save to file the one that will say the following on subject line: ‘’HumbleFax – Successful Transmission to ‘’Provider fax number’’

4. After you submit your request and saved fax/email confirmation of same, proceed to update the status of request on CasePeer by clicking on health providers tab/Medical provider/arrow/type of status update (if only records requested, select ‘’records requested’’ if only billing, select ‘’billing requested’’ if both, select ‘’records and billing requested’’)
5. Lastly, proceed to document your task and set the task due date for 1 week follow up.

  1. **To follow up on previously requested records and bills**

Proceed with the following steps for any requested records and bills by following below steps:

- Step 1:

1. On your task due date, proceed to check on client’s file under Medical folder to see if you have received the requested records and bills. If requested records and bills are already on file, proceed to step 2 but only after reviewing the requested documents to make sure you received the correct ones (Ex. Double checking if it has correct client’s name and DOB and they are indeed the requested reports). Make sure to properly name the reports and bills on file, examples below:
- (DOS 2.8.24) – Initial report_Pagano Chiropractic
- (DOS 2.8.24) – Lumbar MRI_Stand Up MRI
- (DOS 2.8.24)- ER Reports – Lee Memorial
- (DOS 2.8.24) – EMS Report_Lee County BOCC EMS
- (DOS 2.8.24) – Epidural Injection report_Spine and Brain Surgery
- Itemized billing ledger_Spine and Orthopedic Specialists
- Itemized billing ledger_Advanced Diagnostic Group
2. Once you have confirmed the records and bills are received, on file and properly named, proceed to update request status on CP/Health providers/provider name/Arrow/Select desired status.
3. Proceed to add all billing information under providers tab (filling in treatment status (if known), add under Treatment description what client had done, add initial visit date and last visit (if applicable) as well as original bill, adjusted bill, Insurance paid (if payments made by health ins), account #, medpay/pip paid (if known), client paid and still owed information and click save.

4. Proceed to complete your task with note (only if it has been done 100%). If the requested records and bills are not on file, proceed to step 2.

- Step 2:
1. After reviewing client’s file on SharePoint and confirming no records and bills received, proceed to check in records email to see if there are any indications requested documents has been received (if so, proceed to save them on file/naming folder for provider/and naming docs and follow previous steps accordingly as previously described. Refer to: File Distribution Sheet so you know where everything needs to be saved), if not received, call medical facility to follow up on your request. PLEASE do not send another fax/email as a follow-up as there might be a chance, we might have sent the initial request to the wrong fax/email or address and by doing so, it will cause more delays. When contacting the medical facility, always make sure to get the name of the person you spoke with so you can properly document your task with that information.
2. If the reason why you have not received the requested documents is because there is an invoice that needs to be paid first, proceed to add the invoice under Cost tab on client’s case on CP and make sure to task appropriate staff member to issue payment as soon as possible. (Please refer to Staff role description and how to add cost to a case training video). Document your task and set the due date for another week 3 days to make sure payment was made and if so, document your task and move the due date for 3 days to follow up again until records received.
- **Note:** Please make sure to be as detailed as possible when documenting your tasks so it does not leave any room for potential confusion and misunderstandings.
- **Note:** This task due date does not apply when requesting records and bills from Hospitals or Ambulance as those types of requests take a lot longer to be processed.

  2. **How to request Medical record and bills from Ambulance and Hospital – Pending revision**

When a client is seen in a hospital for treatment of their injuries, the Hospital will bill everything separately. The client will have a bill for the emergency room, another bill from the doctor that saw the client and another bill for any imaging or scans done at the hospital. In conclusion, there will be emergency room, ER physician and radiology bill generated. For the ambulance, if client was only seen at the scene of the accident by the Ambulance (EMS) but not transported to Hospital, there will not be a bill for Ambulance, only if client was transported. You can determine if the client transported or not by reading the Ambulance report or looking at the police report.

Some of the requests we submit to Emergency room and/or Ambulance, are handled by a company called Ciox. This company is well known for trying to overcharge 3rd parties like attorneys, to release medical records despite of the request sent to them asks to release electronic records to us and not paper records, therefore, if you are informed you have to submit any request for Hospital records and bills, you MUST follow the next steps:

5. Step 1:

If confirmed your request MUST be sent to Ciox, proceed with steps 1-4 of section I of this procedure (Request medical records and bills for the first time) and then proceed to go to Casepeer to download form labeled as: ‘’Hitech Medical records Ciox’’ to attach to your request and proceed to save on client’s file same way as described on Step 2 from section I of this procedure (Request medical records and bills for the first time).

6. Step 2:

Follow the steps from 6-8 also described on section I section I of this procedure (Request medical records and bills for the first time).

body:
### Procedure how to search businesses or commercial entities on Sunbiz

Whenever we have to locate the registered agent of any companies or corporations to include to name as defendants on any lawsuit or when we have to send letters of representations for any reason, we have to ensure they are addressed to the registered agent of the company or corporation. Any business wanting to operate in Florida must properly register their company or corporation with the secretary of State/Division of corporations. Almost the same applies for other states in the United States (depending on the types of laws they might have). To search any company or corporation information, proceed with the following steps:

- Step 1:

Proceed to visit Florida Department of State/Division of Corporations by visiting dos.fl.gov/sunbiz.

- Step 2:

Once in their website, proceed to click on ‘’Search records’’ and on next window, you can do 2 types of searches depending on the applicable situation which are: 1- Corporations, Limited liability Companies, Limited partnerships, and trademarks. 2- Fictitious Names (when the actual company name might be hidden).

- Step 3:

Search type 1, click on ‘’Name’’ and on next window, proceed to type company name and click on ‘’Search Now’’ as shown on below image:

On the next window, you will have a list of companies with almost same name. You will need to make sure to locate the desire company you are looking for by looking at ‘’Corporate Name’’ column and at ‘’Status’’ (it should have active status) column. Make sure. Please refer to image below:

Note: In this case, the desired company is indicated by arrow as well as the Active status.

- Step 3:

Proceed to click on desired company name with active status. If searching the company or corporation for litigation purposes, on the next window you will need to pay attention to the following:

- If company or corporation is a profit or non-profit organization

- Find the registered agent for the desired company or corporation.

- Step 4:

For search type 2, click on ‘’Fictitious name’’ and on the next window, proceed to type the name of the company you are searching for. When this type of search is required, it is because you were not able to find the correct company or corporation as it might be operating as a d/b/a company and you need to find the real company name. Please refer to the image below.

For this example, we were trying to locate the actual company in which Comcast Corporation is the d/b/a. For this, on the next window, you will proceed to look t Fictitious name/Address/City/Status (and compare to whatever information you have with you to ensure you find the right one). In this case, the following is the right one based on the information I had available at the time:

After clicking on right name, on the next window, I found the correct company name to add to document I needed to work on along with the registered agent I needed to address the document.

- Comcast Business Smartoffice: Actual company name
- Comcast Business Class Security, LLC and mailing address: D/B/A company

1. Send client a CP text asking to please verify email and mailing address.
2. Send SR to attorney assigned as Lead attorney (if no attorney assigned under lad attorney, you will need to send it to the one assigned as…
body:
### Procedures to send SR/CS to clients.

1. Send client a CP text asking to please verify email and mailing address.
2. Send SR to attorney assigned as Lead attorney (if no attorney assigned under lad attorney, you will need to send it to the one assigned as Supervising attorney) along with Police report and declaration pages from the insurance company that put together the release.
3. Document your task and move the task due date for 3 days to f/u on response.

**Note:** If the response from attorney comes with language addition or changes to SR, you will need to f/u with adjuster or OC (adjuster if case was not in litigation and OC if case was in litigation. To determine if case was in litigation or not, you will need to type ‘’Changed case status’’ on Notes search tab on CP. Please refer to Casepeer Status sheet) after sending your request for the SR modifications and f/u with adjuster or OC every 3 days until response obtained. If no answer on your next f/u, you MUST call toll free number if is for an adjuster or call OC law firm to f/u.

4. After approval obtained, proceed to send SR/CS to client for execution via docusign (Please refer to training video for how to do it)
5. Send text message to client to let him/her know you have sent the document via docusign and to please let you know if they have any questions.
6. Document your task and move the due date for 1 week to follow up with client.

Note: On your task due date if client has not responded, you MUST call client to f/u, if no answer, leave a voice message along with a f/u text message. Document task and move due date for another week to f/u.

  1. Copy of new summons

body:
### Once the signed order is received this is what you do next:

1. draft new summons to the secretary of state and file to be issued.
2. Once summons is issued, send through Process Server (Sunbiz) for service with the following:
  1. Copy of new summons
  2. Copy of amended complaint
3. At the same time, and per Florida Statute 48.161(2). Do the following:
  1. Send the below via certified mail w/ return receipt to the last known mailing address of the Defendant:
    1. Copy of new summons
    2. Copy of amended complaint
    3. Copy of Order
    4. Copy of affidavit of diligent search & concealment

NOTE: Receipt must make a copy of the envelope and return receipt and save to sharepoint.

-Update your task once this is mailed, including the tracking number.

4. Once Sumbiz provides the notice of service, immediately file it through the E-Filing portal.
5. Within (before) 40 days of the date of service of the SECRETARY, draft and file Affidavit of Attorney Compliance.
  1. Draft the affidavit of compliance & then send the unsigned copy to reception to prepare a label w/ tracking. This tracking number MUST be added to the affidavit.
  2. Once added to the affidavit, it must be sent to Andrew to sign and notarize. He will then have it scanned into sharepoint.
  3. Proceed to e-file the signed copy & have reception mail to the Defendant’s last known address under the tracking number they previously provided.

NOTE: Affidavit requires attorney signature, so do not wait until the last minute to file this.

6. Draft and file a motion for default

title: Procedures to Contact Unresponsive Clients
summary: It’s imperative for the health of the case to have good open communication with our clients, therefore, this is an especially important part of the case.
body:
### Procedures to handle Unresponsive Clients

It’s imperative for the health of the case to have good open communication with our clients, therefore, this is an especially important part of the case.

The following are the steps we need to follow when contacting a client and what to do if a client does not respond.

- **Step 1:**

Contact client at his/her number on CasePeer. If client does not answer, proceed to leave a detailed voice and text message with your name, where are you calling from, reason for your call and a call back number. On 8x8, proceed to download the call recording of your attempt to contact client (ensure NOT TO MODIFY name of recording once downloaded and instead, just add ‘’number of attempts’’ next to it (i.e. +17868039979-20231024-1st Attempt) and save in client’s file/Contact Attempts (create folder if there is none). After step 1 is completed, go ahead, and update the task assigned to you on CasePeer with everything you did on step 1 and move the task’s due date depending on urgency of said task.

- **Step 2:**

On your task due date, if client has not contacted you back or responded to your text, proceed again with step 1 (exact same way) and this time, proceed to send email client (if available) and add on subject line: Your Case – XXX dol – Contact attempt (i.e. Your Case – 05/03/2022 – 1st Contact attempt) and CC case email ([[case email from CasePeer]](mailto:[case email from CasePeer])) and CC Litigation distro. Proceed to save email confirmation in client’s file/Contact Attempts (create folder if there is none). Document your task due date and move the task due date depending on urgency of said task.

- **Step 3:**

When due date for same task comes, proceed same way as step 1 and 2 and then do the following if you could not get a hold of client again:

- Confirm phone number to be correct by comparing the number on CasePeer against number provided on retainer (if incorrect, correct phone number on CasePeer and proceed with Step 1).

- On CP, check to see if there is any emergency contact information by going to client’s home pag/Click on client’s tab/Look under Contact Details/Emergency Contact. If so, proceed to contact emergency contact same way described on step one and save proof of contact attempt as described on step 1.

- Call medical facility client is treating at (if case is brand new, most likely client is going to chiro/pt, if case is old, try to determine which medical provider client was last seen. Note: download recording of the call same way as described on step 1) to confirm if client is still doing treatment and what phone number do they have in case we were not informed of any phone number changes (update CasePeer if necessary) and try to contact client to number provider might have (making sure to save the recording of the attempt and naming call depending on attempt made, i.e. +17868039979-20231024 – Number provided by medical provider)

- If there is no email information for client, proceed to request from reception a contact letter to be mailed to client’s address. Make sure to save a copy of proof of mailing in client’s file/Contacts Attempts.

- If is a client with co-cases, proceed to contact co-cases to see if they have different contact information for the client and to see if they have seen the client you are trying to reach so they can let client know we need to talk to him/her. (Proceed same way as described on Step 1 regarding recording of phone call)

- Check on signed retainer to see if client provided Employer’s information and if so, google employer and contact them to see if client still works there and if so, if they can provide you with contact information or if we can get a hold of client through employer. (Proceed same way as described on Step 1 regarding recording of phone call. i.e. 17868039979-20231024 – Client’s employer contact attempt)

- Check the police report (if any on file) to see if there is any client phone number provided to the officer and if it is different to the one provided on CasePeer so we can try to call that number. Proceed same way as described on Step 1 regarding recording of phone call. i.e. 17868039979-20231024 – Number on Police Report). Document your task with all steps taken and move the task due date for another week.

- **Step 4:**

On your task due date, proceed to check on your email by adding client’s name to search tab to see if client might have called us back and call went to our answering service, if not, proceed with all previous steps, document your task and move task due date to continue to repeat the previous steps until one month mark. On your task due date for one month mark, proceed with step 4.

- **Step 5:**

After confirming client has not made any contact after all efforts made on steps 1,2,3 and 4 proceed to email team leader (CC amontandon@[firm domain] and management@[firm domain]) informing of the situation and attaching all proof of contact for client and ask if a contact letter with deadline can be mail to client’s last known address. Document your task and move the task due date for one week to follow up on team leader/management instructions and proceed accordingly.

- **Step 6:**

On your task due, if contact letter with deadline approved, proceed to download contact letter from CP/client’s home page/Client contact/contact details tab/envelope/Contact letter with deadline, proceed to request Contact letter with deadline to be mailed Certified mail to client’s last known address (make sure to save word and PDF version with certified tracking number added to letter on clients file). Document your task accordingly and move your task due date for next day to ensure proof of mailing was saved on client’s file and if it was, document task and move due date for 1.5 week to follow up on delivery and any potential contact from client as described on step 5. If on your next task due date client still made no contact with the office, proceed to step 6.

- **Step 7:**

After confirming client has not made any contact after all efforts made, proceed to email team leader (CC amontandon@[firm domain] and management@[firm domain]) informing of the situation and attaching all proof of contact for client so further instructions can be provided. Document your task and move the task due date for one week to follow up on team leader/management instructions and proceed accordingly.

### Litigation Cases - Special Procedures

- Step 1:

For the cases already in litigation and in which deadlines have been violated because for clients being unresponsive to our attempts for contact in which not enough contact attempts evidence collected before based on this procedure, proceed with all previous steps for a full week. Once you come at the end of the week, proceed with Step 5. Document your task and set your task due date for the next day to follow up with team leader.

- Step 2:

On your task due date, if a contact letter with deadline approval is received, proceed the same way described on step 6, document your task and move due date for 1 week to follow up on returned green card and any potential contact from client.

- Step 3:

On your task due date, if no contact attempts from client to us, proceed same way as described on Step 6 and proceed accordingly.

title: Procedures to Inform Clients About a Scheduled IME
summary: An IME is an Independent Medical Examination that might be scheduled for clients by their pip Insurance carrier or in some cases, the insurance company of vehicle client was in at time loss (if client was a passenger …
body:
### c Procedures to inform clients about scheduled IME (Independent Medical Examination)

An IME is an Independent Medical Examination that might be scheduled for clients by their pip Insurance carrier or in some cases, the insurance company of vehicle client was in at time loss (if client was a passenger in the car).

This IME is performed by a medical Doctor of Insurance company’s preference to determine if further medical treatment is necessary or only to certain extend (according to them).

Failure to cooperate or attend this IME may result in possible pip benefits denial, therefore, it’s important to explain to client the importance of attending to same.

The following are the procedures for informing clients about a scheduled IME:

### Note: Check or request for the statutory insurance disclosure

**Note:** in case client says they don't have transportation to attend IME, you MUST call the number provided on IME notification and inform them of same. For example:

Good afternoon, this is XXXX calling from [firm name]. We represent XXX and she/he have an IME scheduled for xxx date but he/she does not have transportation and no way to pay out of pocket for it. Can you please set transportation for client. His/her home address is xxxx.

- **Step 1:**

Set task on Casepeer as: Provide client with IME date, time and location (if task not set on Casepeer) If task already assigned, move to step 2.

- **Step 2:**

Proceed to contact client at the number provided on Casepeer. If client does not answer the phone, proceed with the following:

- Leave a Voice message with your name, where are you calling from and reason for your call and provide a call back number in case client needs to call back.
- Verify phone number is correct on Casepeer by comparing to the one provided on signed retainer located on M/Z drive to ensure we have correct number on file.
- If phone number is correct, proceed to send client a text message with your name, where are you calling from and reason for your call and provide a call back number in case client needs to call back with any questions or concerns.
- **Step 3:** (Only if client did not answer call first time) If client answered, move to step 4

Move task for 2 more days (only if IME is within a few days in advance, if not, move task within 1 day)) to give client a 2nd call to provide IME information. If client does not answer, please follow instructions on step 2.

- **Step 4:** (If client is not going to any of the providers listed below, move to step 5)

If client is going to Pagano Chiropractic, TLC Medical Center or Colonial Post Medical Rehab **ONLY** (clients were referred by these providers to us and we need to ensure they can get paid by pip ins. Carrier to keep a good business relationship), please proceed to email or fax the IME notice (make sure to inform provider they need to let client know about this) and ensure to put fax confirmation on client’s folder under pip carrier’s folder.

- **Step 5:**

After first 3 steps done, proceed with placing detailed update on your task (regarding everything you’ve done on first 4 steps) and move task’s due date to a day before IME’s due date so you can call client to give a friendly reminder.

- **Step 6:**

After all 5 steps fully done, proceed to complete your task with a note (most likely that you reminded client about IME either by text or verbally, whichever applies).

title: Procedures to Set Up New Files in Our System
summary: When a new retainer received, proceed to add name of new client into ‘’New Intakes List – 2022’’ (which can be found on: SharePoint/drive/Clients/Orlando Case Status. Note: Please add new clients on this list directly…
body:
### Intake Department Procedures

  1. **Procedure to set new files on SharePoint**

- Step1:

When a new retainer received, proceed to add name of new client into ‘’New Intakes List – 2022’’ (which can be found on: SharePoint/drive/Clients/Orlando Case Status. Note: Please add new clients on this list directly on SharePoint so it can be always updated.)

- Step 2:

After step 1 completed, proceed to save new retainer on SharePoint, using appropriate template (if case is a single client or are multiple clients) by creating client’s file, using client last name and first name (Ex: Bryant, Casey – if is a single client and Bryant, Casey + 3 – if multiple clients in same accident). If multiple clients in same accident, please refer to step 3.

- Step 3:

If new case involves multiple clients, proceed to create new file as described on step 2 and then, proceed to create every individual case in same folder following the template. Note: if more than 3 clients, just copy and paste folder as ‘’Client’’ as many times as needed.

  2. **Procedures to set up new files on Casepeer**

- Step 1:

Proceed to hit **+** bottom on Casepeer and follow all instructions. Make sure to input every single piece of information provided on retainer. **Note:** Please make sure to add referral source on casepeer, VERY IMPORTANT to do. If referral source not found on drop down list, PLEASE ASK MANAGEMENT SO IT CAN BE ADDED OR PERMISSIOS GRANTED FOR YOU TO BE ABLE TO DO IT.

- Step 2:

Once file is set up, proceed to reassign the tasks automatically set up to appropriate Casepeer user responsible for the handling of said task.

- Step 3:

Proceed to add all Defense and Plaintiff Insurance information (whenever this information is available) and proceed to add medical providers (whenever this information is available) as well.

  3. **Procedures to Set up Auto Claims and send Letter of Representation (LOR)**

Once auto insurance information is available and added on Casepeer, the following steps are to be followed:

- Step 1:

Contact auto insurance company by calling toll free number (phone number added on Casepeer under appropriate section (Defense/Plaintiff) and follow the prompt and instructions to set up claim. (Please refer to procedure as ‘’How to set auto/health insurance subrogation claims’’)

- Step 2:

Once claim has been set up and claim and adjuster info obtained, proceed to add same on Casepeer under appropriate section (Ex. If claim is for BI side, it must be added under Defense Ins. and if claim is for Pip/UM, must be added under Plaintiff Ins.). IMPORTANT: When setting up and obtaining claim information, it is imperative to ask for handling adjuster of claim as follow: for Defense side, always ask for BI and PD adjuster and for Plaintiff side, always ask for Pip and PD adjuster as well.

- Step 3:

Once claim information properly added on Casepeer, proceed to send LORs to appropriate Insurance companies. Please refer to procedures as ‘’How to send Letter of representation to Insurance Companies’’ for proper procedure’s follow up.

- Step 4:

After LOR(s) sent, proceed to complete your task with a note on Caspeer by clicking on ‘’Task bar’’ and clicking on arrow next to task and selecting ‘’Complete task with note’’ (only if task is 100% completed always making sure to add date and your initials to the body of your note.). If task partially completed, please go to step 5.

- Step 5:

If task on casepeer is partially completed, proceed to document your task with all progress made by clicking on ‘’Task tab’’ from client’s file home page on Casepeer and clicking on’’ Edit’’ (Note: it is very important when documenting your task to add the date you are documenting your task along with your initials (Ex: 5/1/22 – AM: xxx) and as much detail as possible) and move task due date for 2 days for proper follow up. You will continue to do your follow ups by moving task due date for every 2 days until task 100% completed

- **Procedures to send LORs to Auto Insurance Companies**

- Step 1:

To send LOR to Defense Insurance, proceed to click on Defense tab on Casepeer and under Adjuster’s tab, click on ‘’arrow’’ and select BI Letter of Representation from drop down list. To send LOR to Plaintiff Insurance, proceed to click on Plaintiff Insurance tab on Casepeer and under Adjuster’s tab, click on ‘’arrow’’ and select Pip Letter of Representation from drop down list.

- Step 2:

After LOR is downloaded, proceed to open it and add any information to it as needed (Ex. Add which VIA is being send (fax, email, USPS mail, etc.) and add all client’s names to it (if LOR is for a case with multiple clients involved).

- Step 3:

Proceed to save LOR (word and PDF version) in client’s file on SharePoint under appropriate sub-folder (Ex. If LOR is for BI/Defense Ins., LOR must be saved on BI Ins. (ensure to rename this folder once you find out who Defense Ins. Is) under ‘’LOR and Fax Conf’’. Same procedure applies for LOR for Plaintiff Ins.

- Step 4:

Once LOR has been saved on client’s file on SharePoint, proceed to send it to appropriate Ins. Company. You MUST then, ensure to save fax/email Confirmation under appropriate folder (Ex. If sending Pip/UM LOR, save confirmation under Pip Ins./LOR and Fax Conf.) once it has been sent.

- Step 5:

After steps 1-4 are completed, proceed to complete your task with note on Casepeer (only if it has been 100% completed). If task partially complete, proceed to step 6.

- Step 6:

When a task to send LORs is partially completed (Ex. we only sent LOR to one of the insurance companies and are pending to send LOR for the other ins. Company because we don’t have the information available yet) proceed to document it with your progress (FYI: all progress must be well documented on Casepeer adding as much detail as possible) and move task due date for 2 more days for proper follow up until you are able to complete your task 100%.

  4. **Procedures how to obtain BI/UM Information.**

Once LOR(s) has been sent, we need to contact Ins. Companies within 2 days to obtain BI/UM limits and status of liability and coverage investigation. Steps as follow:

- Step 1:

To obtain information from BI/Defense Insurance, proceed to contact BI adjuster already added on casepeer. If no adjuster added, proceed to call Insurance Company’s toll-free number and ask for BI and PD adjuster information (Obtain adjuster’s first and last name, phone and fax number and email address (if possible). Same procedure applies for Pip/Plaintiff Ins. Except the adjusters you want to ask for is Pip and PD adjuster.

**Note:** We want to get liability and coverage determination from client’s Ins. (Pip Ins.) only if BI is denying or accepting liability less than 100% as we want to obtain their liability position on the case to know how to proceed with it (either filing law suit if necessary). If liability denied or accepted less than 100%, you must inform your supervisor, attorney or management by sending email to prelit@[firm domain].

- Step 2:

If you were able to speak with adjuster and he/she provided you with BI/UM limits, but status of liability and coverage was still pending at the time you talked to adjuster, proceed to document your task on Caspeer and move your task due date for once a week for proper follow up of this task until 100% complete. If you were not able to speak with adjuster at the time of your call, follow step 3. IMPORTANT: If this is an old task someone else was working on and we still don’t have the information we are looking for; please call toll-free number of insurance company to confirm adjuster’s information. If adjuster is different, proceed to update information on casepeer and follow instructions described on step 1.

- Step 3:

If you were not able to speak with adjuster, leave a voice message (making sure you provide your name, where you are calling from, claim number, reason for your call and best phone number to call you back) and document your task accordingly. Move task due date for 2 more days to allow adjuster time to call back. If after 2 days adjuster has not made contact, please move to step 4.

- Step 4:

If adjuster has not made contact, proceed to call again and follow same procedure as described on Step 3, but this time, make sure to send email/fax advising adjuster what information you are looking for and requesting a call back. Make sure to save your email/fax conf. on file under appropriate sub-folder. Document your task due date for another 2 days for follow up. If still no contact from adjuster at that point, go to step 5.

- Step 5:

If adjuster is unresponsive, proceed to call toll free number and confirm if adjuster you are trying to reach is still the same adjuster assigned (if not, proceed to update information on casepeer and follow same steps) and obtain adjuster’s supervisor’s information and add it on casepeer. If you get confirmation you are attempting to reach the same adjuster, proceed to also contact supervisor and follow same procedures again as described on steps 3-4. If after all steps are properly followed and still not able to obtain information, please send an email to prelit@[firm domain] letting us know about this situation so further instructions can be given. Update your task and move task due day for every 2 days for proper follow up (going through steps 3-5) until 100% completed or new instructions given.

title: First Stage Procedures: Intake
summary: Once client has signed the Agreement of Representation, the procedures are as follow:
body:
### Procedures for First Stage (Intake) of a Personal Injury Case

Once client has signed the Agreement of Representation, the procedures are as follow:

1. Set file on Casepeer and M drive.
2. Set claims with all insurance companies involved and send Letters of Representation to all parties involved. If a Driver License Exchange or Police Report is not available, contact client to see if one can be provided. If unable to reach client, contact Chiropractor’s office as they more likely will have a copy of same. If none of this applies, contact referral source (if no phone number for referral source found, please let Andrew or Ana know immediately, DO NOT WAIT MORE THAN 2 DAYS TO INFORM ABOUT THE SITUATION).
3. If Police Report number given on Agreement of Representation and no DLE available, purchase Police Report online (when applicable).
4. If a commercial vehicle involved and unable to locate Auto Insurance information, the following actions needs to be taken:
- Go on Sunbiz.org and try to locate the Company that the vehicle belongs to.
- Locate Registered Agent and direct LOR to same as ‘’to (name of registered agent) as RA of (name of the company).
- Mail LOR Certified mail (Green Card must be completed, and the name of client must be print in front of Green Card). A task must be set on Casepeer including tracking number to f/u on Green Card withing 5 days and to ensure LOR was received.
5. If no Insurance information provided on Police Report but VIN number was provided, please direct request for search of Auto Insurance information to Ana or Sofia so it can be done on **add123.com**.
6. If no VIN number is available and no insurance information available but Florida License plate of vehicle at fault is available, please direct request for auto insurance inquiry to Ana or Sofia so it can be done on **add123.com**
7. If no Police report available online after 6 days of accident, most likely there won’t be one uploaded online and you must contact the Police Department that attended the scene of accident to find out how to obtain a copy of same. (DO NOT WAIT MORE THAN 6 DAYS TO GET THIS DONE).
8. After file has been set on both sides (Casepeer and M drive), proceed to contact client to do Intake interview and gather all missing information that was not provided on Intake forms and update the file on Casepeer. If client does not answer phone, you MUST leave a voice message and a text message to client so they can return call. Proceed to update your task on Casepeer with the actions you have taken after trying to contact client and DO NOT MARK AS COMPLETED unless you were able to contact client successfully)

### Procedures after file has been set on Casepeer and M drive

Once new file has been set up on both sides, proceed to complete all tasks directed to Intake and these tasks are as follow:

1. Obtain BI and UM limits and status of liability.

(For BI limits, you must contact Defense Insurance. For UM limits, you must contact Plaintiff’s Insurance and liability determination must be obtain from both insurance companies and update Casepeer accordingly with all the information obtained and then proceed to give client an update of their case. Updates to clients should be given at least every three days at this stage).

- Once liability determination has been finalized and is on behalf of our client, you then proceed to assist client with their Property Damage.
- To assist client with their Property Damage, you must contact client and inform him/her about liability determination. You then proceed to obtain from client, vehicle’s location and informing client that they are not to discuss with adjuster anything related to their injuries or prior accidents, only discussion about their property damage. You then contact Defendant’s adjuster and relay the information for inspection purposes. You can let adjuster know that they have authorization to contact our client ONLY IN REGARD TO PROPERTY DAMAGE AND NOTHING ELSE.
2. Follow up on BI and PIP dec pages with respective adjusters.
- Adjusters have, by law, 30 days to response to our request for insurance disclosure (Dec Page) that we sent in our LOR.
- For BI dec page, you must contact defense adjuster to obtain a dec page. For UM dec pages, you must contact plaintiff’s adjuster to obtain a copy of same.
3. Please obtain vehicle estimate and photos and a pip log (New task recently assigned to case plan. You might not see this task for other cases).
- To obtain vehicle estimate and photos you initially must contact defense adjuster as more likely they will be the ones that did the repairs if they have accepted liability (you must verify status of liability if not noted on Casepeer as accepted).
- If defense adjuster does not have vehicle estimate and photos, you then proceed to contact plaintiff’s Property damage adjuster to see if they have one.
- If no vehicle estimates available and you see defense insurance accepted liability, you proceed to contact client and ask if they ever tried to get their vehicle fixed. If the answer was no, you ask client if they want to have their vehicle fixed and if yes, you proceed to contact defense adjuster (just if they accepted liability) to arrange inspection and repairs.
- To obtain a copy of pip log, you must contact plaintiff’s pip adjuster’s insurance to obtain one. (Note: a pip log will be available only within 30 days after treatment has been initiated).
- If you are told after 30 days that there is not a pip log available as there is no bills that were submitted, please proceed to send an email to staff member responsible for setting the file in our database and inform same person that he or she, needs to contact medical provider client is treating and provide them with pip insurance information so they can submit bills to plaintiff’s insurance.
4. Purchase Police report if there is BI or UM coverage.
- This task must be completed by staff member responsible for setting new files in our database.
- A police report should be purchased if there is BI or UM coverage or in cases that a Driver License Exchange was not provided so the case can be properly set up.
5. Intake Client’s Interview
- This task must be completed by staff member responsible for setting file in our database
- There is a series of questions that needs to be asked to clients regarding accident and their medical treatment so we can have as many details regarding case as possible. (Intake interview questions available in other procedures). Once task done, task on Casepeer must be completed with a note.
6. Request Medical Records and Bills
- Staff member responsible for setting new file in our database needs to re-direct this task to staff member responsible for obtaining medical records and bills.
- Once medical facilities added on Casepeer when file is being set up, when reassigning this task, it needs to be more specific (e.x. obtain initial report from XXX medical facility, obtain medical records and bills from Hospital, etc.)
7. Send medical LORs and Welcome letter to client.
- Staff member responsible for setting new file in database must have this task completed.
- Medical LOR and Welcome letter to client can be downloaded on Casepeer.
- Once downloaded, letter must be saved on client’s file and then it must be sent to Medical Facility and to client.
8. Please contact medical provider to find out if client had MRI done already, if so, please obtain MRI report and ledger so client can be set up for Orthopedic Consultation.
- Staff member in charge of setting new files in database, must reassigned this task to staff member in charge of obtaining MRI reports and ledgers and scheduling appointments.

body:
### Litigation Paralegals, Paralegal’s Assistants and Litigation Scheduler’s Role Description

- **Paralegals:**
1. Responsible for researching within cases to draft complaints, summons, plaintiff’s disco to defendant, pre-drafting all case initiation Docs.
2. Responsible for creating new files in the court’s e-portal, for the filing of approved drafted complaint and summons and for saving filling fees on client’s files.
3. Responsible for sending issued summons to process server, tasking assistant and monitor assistant’s performance.
4. Monitors case docket to ensure compliance with court deadlines and tasks assistant accordingly based on case needs.
5. Responsible for monitoring emails sent to litigation email inbox, flagging cases assigned based on CP search, tasking accordingly for very time sensitive matters and urgency and responding to Opposing counsel and firm attorney’s emails pertaining cases assigned.
6. Responsible for the proper drafting of plaintiff’s disco to def. Only.
7. Responsible for the drafting of all Motions
8. Responsible for the scheduling of all hearings for motions.
9. Ensures all CMP deadlines are properly calculated and properly calendared by the assistant.
10. Responsible for properly monitoring all case deadlines and event deadlines to ensure proper compliance with same.

11. Responsible for working with their task's assignments in a timely manner and efficiently and ensuring tasks are not outstanding.
12. Responsible for applying firm’s internal procedures when working with their tasks.
13. Responsible for the supervision of assistant, ensuring the assistant’s task assignment is being worked correctly by assistant based on firm’s internal procedures and coach assistant when otherwise.
14. Responsible for ensuring coordination process of events (depositions, arbitrations, mediation, conference calls) are tasked to litigation scheduler and being worked on based on firm’s procedures.

- **Paralegal’s Assistants:**

1. Responsible for the proper monitoring of email rule ‘’E-service’’, making sure to save all documents coming through that email rule on client’s file, forwarding any motions to litigation attorney and tasking accordingly for any urgent task that should be addressed same day during monitoring of emails.
2. Responsible for proper follow-up of return of service (ROS), and answer to filed complaints as well as for the proper follow up on process server invoices to be saved on file once service is completed.
3. Responsible for drafting replies to complaints and filling of same.
4. Responsible for obtaining approval of drafted plaintiff disco to def., propound, file and follow up on responses and production.
5. Responsible for proper handling of litigation discovery from start to finish from and to defendant after they have been propounded and based on firm’s internal procedures.
6. Responsible for setting task for scheduler to request def. Deposition.
7. Drafts, files, and follows up request for copies from Opposing counsel.
8. Assist paralegal with the correct monitoring of the court docket.
9. Responsible for the proper deadline calculation and calendaring of same.
10. Responsible for drafting, obtaining approval and sending PFS to clients letter as well as for the proper follow up of client’s response on PDF and the filling of PFS acceptance.
11. Works with all tasks assigned to each case efficiently and expeditiously.

- **Litigation Scheduler:**

1. Responsible for the proper monitoring of litigation emails to look for any depositions (plaintiff and def.), CME, mediations, arbitration and conference calls requests from opposing counsel, firm’s attorneys and paralegals as well as the ensuring tasks were assigned accordingly and based on firm’s internal procedures.
2. Responsible for the correct coordination of Depositions (plaintiff and def), mediations, arbitration, CME and conference calls based on firm’s internal procedures.
3. Responsible for saving depositions, mediations, arbitrations, translation services invoices on client’s files and Casepeer, tasking accordingly for payment and follows up until payment is issued and saved on client’s files.

- **Legal Assistant for attorneys**

1. Responsible for coordinating any conference calls requested by attorneys.
2. Reviews files for mediation and prepares mediation binders.
3. Monitors emails and makes sures any client’s request for calls and case updates are handled by respective staff members.
4. Issues medical records payments and process records payments requests from accounting.

title: Setting Motions for Hearings
summary: All motions MUST be set for hearing. (You can ONLY schedule hearings from 9:00 AM until 10:00 A.M.) Follow steps below to set hearings:
body:
### Setting Motions for hearings

All motions MUST be set for hearing. (You can **ONLY** schedule hearings from 9:00 AM until 10:00 A.M.) Follow steps below to set hearings:

### Step 1:

Proceed to send your pre-drafted motion (if applicable). If motion not drafted previously, proceed to download needed template from Casepeer/defense Ins./Adjuster/Envelope/needed motion. Fill in all yellow areas, save word version on client’s file/litigation/Plaintiff and rename document as: Motion (type of motion) _Client’s name. (i.e. Motion for extension of time to serve_Test Case). Proceed to email File motion. Document your task and move your task due date for next day to follow up on approval until it is received (if after 3 attempts to get it approved, on last email (cc office manager and firm owner).

### Step 2:

Once the drafted motion is approved, proceed to file it with the court system, download filed motion and save it on client’s file/litigation/Motions/Plaintiff and rename it as: Filed Motion (type of motion) _client’s name.

### Step 3:

Proceed to look in the docket who is the judge assigned to case and then proceed to do a google search by typing ‘’Judges for xxx county’’ to pull up judge’s internal procedures for hearings (you MUST follow Judge’s internal procedures to set the hearing and proceed accordingly). **Note:** Make sure to include OC (if any) in your correspondence with JA). Go to step 4 for further instructions.

### Step 4:

If the instructions on judge’s internal procedures is to set hearing with JA via email, proceed to request hearing’s proposed dates and times via email from JA and opposing counsel, making sure to attached filed motion (ONLY if judge’s internal procedure allows this) and on body of email ask for available dates and times to set the hearing. On subject line, add: Case style name (as it appears on court docket) – Hearing request. Document your task and set a due date for 3 days to follow up on proposed dates. If no dates are available on your task due date, proceed to forward initial email to JA and OC and on same subject line add number of follow ups (i.e. Case style name (as it appears on court docket) – Hearing request – 1st follow up). Document your task and move for another 3 days to continue to follow up until dates provided.

### Step 6:

Once proposed dates provided by JA, proceed to check your attorney’s calendar to check availability for those dates. (if those dates are not available, check for at least 4 dates and times and get back to JA and OC with new proposed dates, document task and set due date for 3 days to follow up on agreed date). If attorney available for any of those dates, proceed to block one date by adding the following: (First name and initials of your last name)**HOLD** – Hearing for Motion (type of motion)_Client’s name and DOL (i.e. (John B.)**HOLD** – Hearing for Motion for Extension of time to serve_ Case, Test - DOL 05/04/2022) and by highlighting the slot for number of hours needed depending on the motion that will be heard. Also add on body of event what type of hearing it is (i.e. Hearing for Motion for Extension of time to serve defendant, etc).

**Note:** if the hearing is for Motion to Dismiss, Motion for Summary judgment, Motion for Judicial’ s default, Motion for sanctions, Motion to stay, you need to block slot for 1.5 hour. Rest of Motions you block for 1 hour.

### Step 7:

Once you have calendared the hearing, proceed to draft notice of hearing, by downloading it from casepeer/home page/defense insurance/adjuster/envelope icon/Notice of Service (type of notice). Rename it to NOS for (type of notice) _Client’s name (i.e. NOS Motion for Extension of time to serve defendant). Send it to litigation or consultant for approval. Document task and move due date for 1 day for follow up on approval until done.

### Step 8:

Once Notice of Service approved, proceed to file it and save filed copy on client’s file/litigation/Notices/Plaintiff. Complete your task with a note.
