### Procedure – Clearing Case Calendar

1. For cases with deposition confirmed (for plaintiff):
- Check the court docket to look for filed NOVD.
- Once NOVD filed, email filed NOVD to OC (cc litigation email) with the following email content:

Thanks in advance.

- Document your task and move your task due date for 2 days to follow up on OC reply to your initial email. If no reply, forward initial email to them applying previous steps and this time, add the following on body of your email:

Good morning/Afternoon,

Please accept this email as a friendly reminder that our client has filed NOVD. Please confirm receipt of the email below.

Thank you.

- Proceed to remove deposition event from CP and Outlook calendar along with all calendared deadlines.
- Complete your task with notes.

2. For cases with depositions request (Plaintiff/Defendant’s depo) and CMEs:
- Procced to check on Lawsuit Dismissal project list if case is added under ‘’Low Value Cases’’ or ‘’Liability Denials cases’’’ . If case appears under ‘’Low Value Cases’’, check the Notes column to see if anyone is working on that case and if not, proceed to add a note (making sure to add the date and your initials) and assigned one of the working team to it (Carlos, Jeffrey or Karla) and then proceed to assigned task to one of them on Casepeer due for very next day as follow: Please contact client to get authority to dismiss.
- If the case appears under ‘’Liability denials’, proceed to email attorney associate (Adam Jacobson) (cc litigation email) as well as an 8x8 text asking to review case and provide instructions if we will withdraw from case or not and until response received, we need to leave task open (and adding notes under task) and moving task due date until our motion to withdraw is heard by the judge continue to follow up on the coordination task with OC.
- After the motion is heard by the judge and hearing coordinator updates your tasks with notes that motion was granted, you then proceed to complete your tasks with notes. If the motion was not granted, follow up with attorney associate using same initial email you sent before. Document your task and move the task due date for 2 days to follow up.
- If a CME was already coordinated and a videographer was hired, we need to make sure we cancel the videographer request.
- After all; above is done, proceed to clear calendar in CP and outlook along with all case deadlines.

title: File Review for Demands and Reductions
summary: This is the procedure that described everything involved in the closing of the case which is the final stage of a Personal Injury case. It all starts with the proper review of the file to prepare the case for closing,…
body:
### Procedure – Demand and reductions file review for cases with: Litigation, Pre-Suit and Pending Demand casepeer status.

This is the procedure that described everything involved in the closing of the case which is the final stage of a Personal Injury case. It all starts with the proper review of the file to prepare the case for closing, which consist of the collection of client’s medical records and bills and all supporting evidence to prove the damages caused by tortfeasor’s negligence which gets summited in our demand packet. At the same time of that review, we also need to review the cases for the medical bills reduction process so client can make a more informed decision regarding settlement of their case. Please follow the steps below for the proper review for demand and reductions:

- **1- Demand Review:**

The way the demand packet will be addressed will depend on the status of the case since a lot of the cases are already in litigation and a good number of them are not. When a case is already in litigation, more likely the demand packet will need to be addressed to opposing counsel if one is already assigned from the defense Ins. side. If not, the demand packet is then addressed to adjuster from Insurance company. To review a file for demand, proceed with the following steps:

- **Step 1:**
1. Proceed to open case on Casepeer and Sharepoint.
2. On casepeer, proceed to assign your name as ‘’Lien negotiator’’ to the file and any linked cases (if applicable) and verify case status to determine who the demand packet needs to be addressed to (Opposing counsel or Ins. adjuster). **Note:** To determine if the demand packet needs to be addressed to an opposing counsel, on sharepoint, proceed to check folders: Litigation/Complaint and Summons/Answer to affirmative defenses and reply/Answer. If an answer has been saved on SP, please refer to Exhibit A on this procedure to see how an answer looks like and where to obtain Opposing counsel’s information and proceed to add Opposing counsel firm and attorney on CP. (Please refer to procedure – How to add legal representation under Defendant.)
3. Proceed to verify the Ins. Companies added on CP, status of liability and coverage and policy limits from Defense Ins. as well as policy limits from plaintiff Ins. (if any), to determine the type of demand needed (BI/UM demand) and to which Ins. company we are sending a demand to.

**For Cases with a Pending Demand status:** if there is BI and UM coverage on the case, we MUST send demand to both Ins. Carriers if one of the following criteria is met:

- Client’s outstanding medical bills EXCEED BI limits. *(This part will be a lot easier to determine once you have prepared net sheet)*
- BI Limits are low or almost equal to client’s outstanding medical bills.

**For Cases with Litigation Status ONLY:** If there is UM coverage available but the client’s total outstanding medical bills DOES NOT EXCEED BI coverage, we will not send an UM Demand packet AT ALL. *(This part will be a lot easier to determine once you have prepared net sheet)*

- **Step 2:**
1. After step 1 is completed, proceed to sharepoint to start the review process.
2. Proceed to prepare net sheet (Please refer to Exhibits on this procedure so you know how a net sheet looks like and please refer to: Procedure - How to prepare client’s Net Sheet included on this master procedure so you know how to prepare it correctly) by using the most recent net sheet version dated 2/3/24. **Note:** There is a net sheet already added to the file, however, we have updated same, and we must use the most recent one as stated before.
3. Once you have started the preparation of your net sheet, proceed with the review of the file which is done in the following 2 stages:

- **Stage 1**
1. Check Casepeer: Verify information obtained during intake interview (on incident description), details of that interview so you can see if client might have gone to ER by EMS or went to ER days after accident, if client had any prior attorneys we should know of, any potential workers compensation liens, etc. Note: Proceed to download Demand Checklist from Casepeer/Defense-Plaintiff Ins. tab/adjuster tab/Demand checklist and start working on same as well. Save copy on client’s file/demand and settlement folder/demand packet and continue to fill it out as you continue your review and make your proper follow ups to ensure you don’t forget anything. You will need to sign and date this checklist before sending your demand letter for approval.
2. Police Report: Verify if client was transported to Hospital by EMS, or if client was treated at scene of accident by EMS. If transported, we MUST obtain reports and bills from EMS and ER.

**Note:** if client was seen by EMS at scene of accident but WAS NOT transported, THERE WON’T BE A BILL for EMS, therefore, a task to get EMS bill SHOULD NOT BE assigned.

3. Review Dec Pages for both Ins. Companies: verify the Ins. disclosures from both Ins. companies are on file by confirming we have the following documents (please refer to exhibit on this procedures):

For Defense Ins.

- Affidavit of Coverage
- Affidavit of Additional Ins. (Executed. If not on file, we only do 3 follow ups and close task)
- Declaration Pages

For Plaintiff Ins.

- Affidavit of Coverage
- Declaration Pages
- UM Selection/rejection form

If some of the above documents are missing, a task MUST be assigned to an appropriate staff member to obtain it. (Please refer to: Staff Role description sheet for this)

4. Property Damage: verify we have vehicle estimate, total loss evaluation (when applicable) and any supplemental estimate and photos (if applicable). Make sure vehicle estimate belongs to our client’s vehicle (or owner of vehicle client was driving if client was not the owner) or to owner of vehicle we are representing. – Task accordingly if missing.

**Note:** Vehicle estimate with less than $1,000 dollars, WON’T BE included in demand packet.

5. Prior Attorney Folder: verify that folder to see if there is any prior attorney termination letter signed. If there is, you need to double check if signed termination letter was sent to prior attorney by looking for confirmation by fax/email and proof of mailing as well. If no signed termination letter, you need to set up task to VA responsible for having client sign one and task to whoever needs to send it to prior attorney and Ins Company.
6. Review Intake folder: verify that we have signed retainer, client’s ID, any health Ins. card (when applicable), any ER discharge papers (if any) and any other important information/documents deemed necessary to work on the case. If any of these items are missing, you need to set a task to responsible VA to request this from client.
7. Advance/Pre-Settlement Folder: If client took funding, task accordingly to obtain a payoff letter and ensure funding was added on CP, if not, proceed to add.

**Note:** Look for any other folders added to add information to net sheet and task accordingly (Ex. Child Support Lien, Workers Compensation Lien, med pay lien, etc.)

- **1.1 – Reductions review**

- **Stage 2 (For this review, please refer to ‘’Checklist of items included in demand packet’’)**

For this stage review, you MUST start organizing the demand packet in chronological order by adding a copy of all documents needed on a demand packet as well as adding all medical and any liens information to net sheet as you go through the review of the case during stage 2. **Note:** During this part of the review, you will also be reviewing the file for reductions at the same time. You will need to make sure to add on CP all billing information (total charges, payment, balance owed, etc), date of visit and brief treatment description under ‘’Treatment description’ section in CP (Ex. Emergency room for ER, ER physician, Lumbar and Cervical MRI for MRI facility, etc). You will also be adding all billing information and estimated reduction numbers as you go through your review on the net sheet. A sheet containing all medical procedures and potential reduction estimates scenarios will be added to this procedure for guidance as to how to produce reduction estimates on cases so the max offers can be added to it during your review. Start the review on this stage as follow:

1. Pip log: ensure we have the most recent pip log on file. Pip logs more than 60 days old, **A NEW ONE MUST BE OBTAINED!** Proceed to properly review pip log to ensure ALL medical providers were added to client’s file and also to properly add pip payments to net sheet as you go through your review.

**Note:** For demand packets of cases in litigation, we don’t need to wait for an updated pip log to send demand packet out, but we still need to task to get updated pip log. For cases in litigation, we will not provide a copy of a pip log.

2. EMS (if applicable to case): ensure we have EMS report and itemized ledger. (We don’t reduce this bill and we always pay it in full)
3. Emergency Room Treatment (if applicable to case): ensure we have emergency room reports (not discharge records) and ER, ER physician and radiology billing ledger and that records are indeed for a DOS related to the accident.

**Note:** To determine if ER visits are related to accidents or not, on ER reports, look for ‘’Chief complaint’’ or for the reason of the visit. If no report of any MVA (Motor Vehicle Accident), then more likely that particular visit is not related to accident and should not be included in demand packet. (We normally don’t reduce any of the ER bills UNLESS the client will be upside down. This is why making sure DOS listed on reports is accident related. Also check all ER ledgers to look for any potential health insurance payments and if there is any, same MUST be added to net sheet under Health Subro lien and a final lien letter amount MUST be obtained because they are entitled to reimbursement of any payments made on behalf of the client when bills are liability related and there is potential recovery of same).

4. For Chiropractic/PT Treatment: ensure we have initial report, soap notes, final report, and itemized billing ledger. Verify all reports received are current accident related and not from another MVA sent to us by mistake. It is very important to pay attention to this part as this will negatively impact the outcome of the case when is time to settle it with OC/Adjuster.

**Note:** You MUST go through entire records/bills received from provider as they will normally send us the entire patient chart which will often contain other providers reports (Ex. EMC, X-rays, MRI, testing, etc.) which WE MUST obtain billing ledgers to include in demand packet for those providers.

5. EMC Evaluation: ensure we have EMC report and itemized billing ledger.
6. MRIs: ensure MRI reports and itemized ledgers are on file (make sure to review ledger to ensure no other MRI reports are missing or non-accident-related DOS are listed. If so, you need to task staff member to request from provider to remove all non-accident related from that ledger as this can cause issues during settlement of the case).
7. Orthopedic Treatment: ensure we have all Orthopedic reports (Orthopedic reports must be reviewed to safeguard the health of the case) and current itemized ledger. **Note:** When reviewing Ortho reports, verify correct DOL is on report, check reports and look for any indications clients might have reported to provider they went to any Emergency Room/Urgent Care visit for which we might have no knowledge of, any potential new MRIs, etc. When reviewing the current itemized ledger, confirm we are not missing any reports by comparing all DOS (Date of Service) on the ledger versus reports in our possession. Task accordingly if we are missing any.
8. Medical Clearance Records and bills for surgeries (if applicable to case): ensure we have medical clearance reports, chest x-ray report, EKG report, itemized billing ledger, etc.
9. Itemized Surgical Bills (if applicable to case): ensure we have surgical facility itemized billing ledger, anesthesia billing ledger, any medical supplies invoices (when applicable), surgery assistants (when applicable), brace invoices (when applicable), etc. these types of bills are extremely high, and we CAN’T send a case in demand WITHOUT them. Please refer to the demand checklist of items included in the demand packet for your reference on which procedures are considered actual surgeries and injections and which ones are not.
10. Medical transportation Itemized bill (when applicable):
11. Any case cost and expenses must be added to net sheet during this part of the review (any litigation cost and prelitigation expenses as well – Please refer to training video: How to review files for demand and reductions). **Notes:** all expenses must be added on Casepeer and all invoices in which you don’t see a receipt for payment, must be tasked to appropriate staff member responsible for the payment of same so they can be paid off, more specifically the invoices for medical records/bills request.

### Step 3:

Once your review has been completed, proceed to document your task with the findings of your review (it is easier to follow your task if you document it in the form of a checklist for anything pending) and move your task due day to follow up for 1 week. Then, proceed to task appropriate staff members accordingly to obtain all missing documents for demand packet (please refer to ‘Staff and role description’ sheet) and set their task due date for the very next day. Proceed to save Net sheet on client’s file/Demand and Settlement folder/Settlement/Bill reductions and net sheet.

### Step 4:

On your task due date to follow up, proceed to check case on SP (Sharepoint) to look for receipt of missing items. If none of them are on file, please proceed with Step 5. If items are already on file, please proceed to Step 6.

### Step 5:

If after a week, the pending documents are still not on file, check appropriate’ s staff member task to see the reason why we are still pending the documents. If the reason why staff member responsible for obtaining the pending docs is related to any potential negligence in their part or improper handling of the task, you MUST email team leader along with case name so they can be coached on how to do it correctly or emphasis the urgent need for the task to be completed. Proceed to document your task and move your task due date for another week for follow up.

### Step 6:

After all missing documents are already on file, proceed to finish filling out demand checklist by initializing all areas applicable to the case you reviewed and sign and date at top of checklist sheet and make a copy of missing docs to demand packet previously organized (if not, organized them in treatment chronological order) and update net sheet. At this point, proceed to finish your reduction review estimate by producing the max offers for each provider (based on sheet attached). As soon as this is done, proceed to draft demand letter (Please go to step 7 and forward to know how to get this done).

### Step 7: (BI-UM Demands)

To draft a BI demand letter, proceed to CP (Casepeer) and from client’s file Home page, proceed to click on ‘’’Defense Insurance’’

On next screen, proceed to call Insurance Company’s toll-free number located on Ins. Company ‘’Phone’’ to confirm BI handling adjuster. For this step, you will need to provide a representative with the claim number, our client’s name and DOL. You then ask for BI handling adjuster’s first and last name, phone number and email address (if any). If the adjuster is different than what we previously had, you then proceed to add a new adjuster on CP. Please refer to the images below to know how to do it.

To call toll-free number:

To add new handling adjuster, click on ‘Arrow’ icon:

From drop down list, select ‘’Edit’’

On next screen, proceed to go to slot depending on the handling adjuster you are looking to add. **Note:** to ensure we are not duplicating adjuster’s information, type name of new adjuster information on desired tab and if the name comes up on the drop-down list, select correct name and ensure contact information is the same by clicking on ‘Edit’ and then ‘Save’ if nothing needed to be added or modify. In this case, new BI adjuster will be added by clicking on ‘Add’. **Note:** If you need to add UM Adjuster, since there is not a slot for that specific one, this can be added under ‘’Medpay/Pip supervisor’ and under note tab, you add note as: UM Adjuster handling that particular client’s claim.

On next screen, we will fill out all designated tabs to add new adjuster’s Information and then click ‘Save’:

Proceed to draft BI demand letter by clicking on ‘Envelope’ And from drop down list, select ‘BI Demand letter’

This action will prompt a demand letter to be downloaded and filled with client’s and adjuster’s information. For opposing counsel information will need to be added manually to the demand letter. (Please refer to Exhibits for an example of a demand letter). On demand letters already downloaded, proceed to add all medical bills from all providers which were already added on net sheet. Once this part is done, then proceed to add the demand response deadline, save the demand letter and upload it to SP and email copy of demand packet along with demand letter and signed and initialized checklist to attorney for review, further instructions or approval (CC pre-lit email and team leader).

For UM demands, apply the same instructions previously explained in step 7, with the ONLY difference that instead of clicking on Defense Ins., you MUST click on Plaintiff Ins. When drafting UM demand letter, proceed with same instructions previously given.

**Note:** demand response deadline for cases Pending Demand and NOT in litigation will always be 14 days.

**Note:** for demand response deadline for cases in Litigation, wait for instructions from attorney reviewing and approving demand.

Once all of the above done, proceed to document your task and move task due date for next day to follow up on attorney’s response. Move to step 9.

### Step 8:

If case was in litigation and OC already assigned, you then need to add OC on CP by Clicking on Defense Insurance as previously shown, and then clicking on ‘’Legal Representation’’ then on ‘Arrow’ and on ‘Edit’ from drop down list and after everything has been filled out, then click ‘Save’.

On next screen, proceed to add OC information and handling attorney on designated slots indicated in following picture by arrows, making sure to add law firm first to ensure we are not duplicating information.

### Step 9:

1. On your task due date and after approval from attorney, proceed to send demand packet to adjuster or OC from Ins. Companie (BI/UM – when applicable) via email ONLY if one is available. If no email is available, then a request to mail a CD containing a demand packet MUST be made to reception via email. Make sure to add on subject line: OUTGOING MAIL REQUEST – Demand packet – Client’s name and DOL and CC prelit at all times. (Note: If you requested demand packet to be mail out, make sure reception did this by checking the Proof of mailing items’’ folder in SP and look for the scanned envelope of the demand, if none on file, follow up with reception)

2. After confirmation demand has been sent, proceed to send the demand on CP as well by going under Settlement tab on left column of case/click on Settlement proceeds arrow/select what type of demand was sent based on CP information (Defense – third party/Plaintiff – UM Demand)/Defendant Ins – pick desired one/click policy limits option/select date sent/select date expires (deadline to respond to demand) and click save. Refer to pictures below:

Make sure fee logic is set to 33.33% (if an answer to complaint was not filed) or to 40% (if one was filed). If you need to change fee logic, click on arrow next to demand information and select ‘’Edit fee logic’’

### Step 10:

After step 9 completed, proceed to complete your task with the note of everything done and proceed with the following:

- If the case has any litigation status on CP (Please refer to case status sheet), DO NOT CHANGE STATUS TO ANYTHING and proceed to assign the following tasks to appropriate staff member:
1. Follow up with adjuster to ensure demand was received. Task due date set within 3 days of sending demand.
2. Follow up on demand response from Adjuster/OC. Task due date set same day demand response is due. If adjusters request extensions, please have them email supervising/litigation attorney.
- If the case is not in litigation, proceed to change status to Demanded and re-assign the following tasks to yourself with correct due dates:
1. Follow up with adjuster to ensure demand was received. Task due date set within 3 days of sending demand.
2. Follow up on demand response from Adjuster. Task due date set same day demand response is due. If adjuster requesting extensions, please have them email supervising attorney.

**Step 11: - For closing specialists’ assistant**

1. Proceed to follow designated tasks assigned. If for whatever reason adjuster/OC claims they did not receive demand packet, proceed to task closing specialists asking to send new demand out and ensure you move the task to follow up on response for the correct due date. But if an actual response received (please ensure response is in writing and saved on SP), then those 2 previous tasks must be 100% completed and proceed with the following:

- **For cases in Litigation:**

2. Proceed to assign the following task to lien negotiator assigned to case:

***Please review file for reductions and inform supervising attorney by email (please copy prelit email) once reductions estimate available***

2. Proceed to add settlement offer on CP by going to Settlement tab/Click on arow next to Ins. Company name/select Add offer/Offer date and click save.

3. Then send email to attorney that approved demand informing of demand response for further handling WIHTOUT CHANGING CP STATUS.

- **For cases NOT in Litigation:**

4. Repeat the exact same process as outlined above to this one, with the exception that you WILL CHANGE STATUS TO SETTLEMENT NEGOTIATIONS. In this case, you don’t need to manually add a task for Lien Negotiator because the following task will automatically be assigned with a due date of next date if lien negotiator was previously assigned and before status changed:

***Please review file for reductions and inform supervising attorney by email (please copy prelit email) once reductions estimate available***

body:
### Procedure: How to e-file new lawsuits and pleadings

1. Go to myflcourtaccess.com.
2. Log in.
3. Click on e-filing map located at the top right of the window.
4. Under ‘’Select File Jurisdiction/Trial Court/Click on Case Initiation (when filling new lawsuit)/File document(s) on Existing Case to Clerk (when filling any pleadings on an existing case)
5. Select County from drop down menu and click File Now
6. Fill in all case information for:
- Case information:

County: Make sure correct county is selected. 
Division - always circuit civil
Case type - other negligence (usually always this)
Sub type - auto negligence (for auto accidents) premises liability (for slip & fall and premises liability cases) other negligence (for cases that are not auto accidents or premises liability cases)

Total Number of Defendants: 
Proceeding type of case - same as sub type
Complex business court indicator - always no
Remedies sought - always monetary
Amount of claim - always $50k-75k (don’t pick anything else)
Number of causes of action - how many counts are on complaint
Class action - always no
Related case field - always no
Jury trial demanded - always YES
Involves allegations of Sexual Abuse - always no

After filling in all tabs, proceed to click ‘’Next’’

7. Proceed to create all parties involved in the lawsuit:
- Case parties:

Click on ‘’Add party’’

Role/select Plaintiff/select Primary Party and Filed on Behalf of (this will be the first name that will appear in the lawsuit. The name should be the lead case (i.e. driver of the vehicle – when there are multiple plaintiffs). Note: Have your drafted and approved complaint and summons when creating parties so you can refer to them using the address and correct names. Use client’s address on CP when creating Plaintiff.

Proceed to add plaintiff’s first and last name and address and then click ‘’Save’’

When adding defendant, proceed same way as previously described: click on Add party/Role/defendant/Defendants name and last name and address (if a person) Company name and address (if a company under ‘’OR Organization) Put in every plaintiff & every defendant and then click Next.

8. Proceed to upload all pleadings:
- Documents:

Check auto generated civil cover sheet to make sure all case info is right.

Click on Add/Find the document type you need to file on search tab (i.e. complaint, Summons, Notice of Service of interrogatories, Request for production, Notice of Service of Interrogatories, Request for admissions, etc)/upload your document/click save. Note: to add rest of pleadings, repeat previous steps until all of them are done.

On confidentiality option, click on option (a) nd then click next.

9. Service List

Under Electronic Service Recipients/select Serve all? And click next.

10. Fees and Payments

Under Payments/Select One to Continue/click on Option One: Provide Payment Information/Previously saved payments/Saved Credit Cards/(the firm's saved card)/Click next at the bottom of window.

11. Review and submit

Review everything done before and proceed to click on save.

body:
### Procedure – How to process Motion to Withdraw (constructive lien and without lien)

- **For attorneys ONLY – For cases for Motion to withdraw without lien**
1. Proceed to open case on Sharepoint and Casepeer.
2. Proceed to assigned task to yourself as: *Review file for withdrawal* and proceed to check the Police report to review case from the liability standpoint (more specifically to see if we have correct liability denial and not a situation in which casepeer simply grabbed the wrong information). If this is the case, proceed to highlight the case in ‘’Yellow’’ and set it aside. Highlight the cases with following colors for below scenarios:

- Potential for settlement – Color: Light green

- Sovereign cases with 768 letters sent – Color: light blue

- Sovereign cases without 768 letters sent – Color: light orange

3. Once you have determine the case indeed has a liability issue, proceed to call client to explain we have decided to withdraw from their case given the circumstances of the liability part and ask client if they would like to keep their case open and if so, explain they will then need to start looking for a new attorney to take their case immediately because as soon as Judge grants our withdrawal they will only have certain amount of time to continue to pursue litigation on their case. **Note:** Please follow below notes whichever applies:

- Ask client if they would like to pursue their lawsuit against tortfeasor, if they say yes, proceed with next notes, if they say they don't want to continue to pursue it, proceed to briefly explain the dismissal repercussions and obtain recorded consent for the dismissal of the lawsuit (please refer to Procedure – Filling Notice of Voluntary Dismissal without prejudice – Step 3 and follow the instructions) and proceed to assign the following task to appropriate staff member (Mary De Luna temporarily): *Please draft, get approval and file NOVD an*d document that task with your conversation with client.

- Be sure to inform our client we will need signed agreement from them to withdraw from their case so we can avoid a hearing with the Judge, otherwise, they will need to attend that important hearing with the Judge which makes the process more complicated. Confirm client’s email and mailing address at the time and proceed to task (Mary De Luna temporarily) as follow: *Please obtain signed agreement from client for attorney withdrawal.*

4. After speaking with client, change status on casepeer to ‘’Pending drop’’ (please be careful of the cases with multiple plaintiffs since you will need to determine if we are withdrawing from all of them and if not, to ensure the status only changes to that one.) and proceed to complete your task with all proper documentation of everything done (Please review file for drop)
5. Re-assign the following auto generated tasks to appropriate staff member based on the staff role description:
- Please draft, get approval and file Motion to Withdraw (if applicable to case). If not applicable to case, please complete this task with notes. (*re-assign to Mary De Luna temporarily until we are done with all cases we need to withdraw from. After that, it needs to be re-assigned to paralegal assigned to case)*

- Please send Attorney withdrawal letter to all parties. For client’s withdrawal letter, send it along with signed order (when applicable). Thank you (Please refer to staff role description)

- **For legal assistant – ONLY**

6. **For MIA clients cases (Motion to withdraw – With Lien):** Draft Motion to withdraw along with Notice of Asserting attorney Lien (both can be downloaded from CP/Defense Ins/Adjuster), double check your work, save it on client’s file/Litigation/Motions (the motion) Notices (for the notice)/Plaintiff and send it for approval to litapprovals@[firm domain].

**For cases in which we are simply withdrawing from the case without asserting lien (Motion to withdraw – No lien):** Apply same procedure except you are not drafting and filling any Notice of asserting attorney lien. **Note:** If you see the following task assigned with notes:

  - *Please draft, get approval and file NOVD*
  - *Please obtain signed agreement from client for attorney withdrawal.*

Drafting, obtaining approval and filing Motion to Withdrawal WILL NOT BE necessary. Instead, you will either draft, obtain approval and file NOVD or you will draft the agreed Order

(whichever applies). Ensure recorded authority was saved on client’s file/Litigation/Consent to dismiss, if not, please email staff member that assigned task to you asking to please upload the recording to client’s file- Needs to be reviewed by Payton

Document your task and move the task due date for 2 days to follow up. (**Note:** this needs to be approved ASAP).

7. On your task due date and after your Motion to withdraw has been approved, proceed to file same and set it for hearing. (Please refer to procedure – How to set motions for hearing).
8. After you have coordinated hearing with all parties, proceed to draft your Notice of hearing (you will find it on CP/Defense Ins/Adjuster tab), fill in all information needed, double check your work, save on client’s file/Litigation/Notices/Plaintiff and send it for approval to litapprovals@[firm domain]. Document your task and set the due date for 2 days. (Make sure to add event on outlook and CP calendar and add attending attorney for it).
9. On your task due date and after your notice is approved, proceed to file same and make sure to save filed copy on client’s file/Litigation/Notices/Plaintiff.
10. Proceed to send the filed Motion to withdraw, notice of charging attorney lien (if applicable) and Notice of hearing to client via email (make sure to save the email confirmation on clients file) and also via certified mail (make sure reception saved proof of mailing on client’s file). Document your task with everything done and set the task due date for the same day of hearing.
11. Be sure to check the Judge’s procedures in the event you need to send them the Notice of Hearing.
12. After hearing, check to see if any notes were added under your task by the attorney attending hearing and if not, proceed to email that attorney asking what the Judge said so you can proceed with drafting Order. (cc litigation@[firm domain]).
13. After you have gathered the information from the attorney, proceed to draft your Order (check Judge’s procedure to see if they have their own Prder template and if not, proceed to download template from CP/Defense Ins/Adjuster/Order). Fill out the Order with all hearing information, double check work, save on client’s file/litigation/Orders and send to attorney that attended the hearing for approval. Document your task and set the date for 2 days to follow up.
14. On your task due date and after the order has been approved, proceed to file same and make sure to save filed copy on client’s file same location as before. Document your task and set a due date for 2 days to follow up on the signed order.
15. On your task due date and after signed Order available, proceed to save signed order on client’s file/litigation/orders. Complete your task with notes and proceed to add notes under the last automated task. Informing signed order on file.

title: Personal Injury Litigation: General Phases and Description
summary: A PI case will generally go into the litigation phase for the following reasons:
body:
### PI Litigation General Phases and Description

A PI case will generally go into the litigation phase for the following reasons:

- We were not able to achieve an amicable agreement to settle the case during pre-litigation phase.
- We disagree with the insurance companies’ liability determination (decision made by a licensed attorney ONLY)
- If the case is against a governmental entity, slip and fall, premises liability, etc.

Below are the general common steps in the litigation phase which is dictated by Florida Rules of Civil Procedures:

1. **Initiation of the lawsuit**

The first step to initiate the litigation process is the drafting and filing of the complaint and summons. Part of the firm’s strategy during the initiation of the lawsuit, is also the drafting and filing of plaintiff’s discovery request to defendant along with deposition request to depose the defendant. *Please refer ‘’Procedure – Initiation of the lawsuit’’*

- Task to file lawsuit (for paralegal and based on firm’s procedures)

2. **Service of pleadings**

This is the process of notifying defendants a lawsuit has been filed against them by handing filed pleadings (filed complaint, stamped summons, plaintiff disco to defendant and deposition request) by process server (individual personally handing filed pleadings to defendants). **COURT DEADLINE:** Plaintiff has 120 days to serve all defendants from time initial complaint was filed. *Please refer to ‘’Procedure – Service of pleadings’’*

- Task to file lawsuit (for paralegal and based on firm’s procedures)
- Task to follow up on Return of service (for assistant and based on firm’s procedures)
- Task to calendar lawsuit deadlines (for assistant - based on any court CMP or Agreed filed CMP)

3. **Pending response**

This is the next step which means plaintiff waits for filed Answer to Complaint and Affirmative defenses, responses to plaintiff disco to defendant done by defense counsel after defendant have been served. **COURT DEADLINE:** Defendants have only 20 calendar days from the time service was done. *Please refer to ‘’Procedure – Pending Response.*

- Task to file lawsuit (Needs to be completed with notes – if applicable **Note:** this task remains open through filing Plaintiff’s Reply to Defendant’s Answer AND through any motion for defaults and subsequent hearings)
- Task to draft Plaintiff Disco to Def (for paralegals and based on firm’s procedures)
- Task to follow up on Return of service (for assistant – should be completed with notes when applicable and based on firm’s procedures)
- Task to respond to Def. Disco (for assistant and based on firm's procedures)
- Task to follow up with def. On plaintiff disco responses (for assistant and based on firm’s procedures)

4. **Litigation Discovery**

This is the phase of the case in which both sides are gathering their evidence for a potential trial. We propound discovery on Opposing Counsel when they propound us with discovery, depositions and mediations can not be scheduled without discovery being responded to, particularly Plaintiff’s discovery responses. There is also a Court deadline to propound our initial discovery request. Please refer to ‘’ Drafting Discovery Responses Propounded by OC’’ to process Opposing counsel litigation discovery. **COURT DEADLINE:** both partis have a 30-day deadline to respond to Discovery **if** disco was not propounded during initiation of the lawsuit. If **it** was, then there is 45 day deadline Defendant’s discovery. Defendant – *Please refer to ‘’Procedure – Litigation Discovery’’*

- Task to draft Plaintiff Disco to Def (for paralegals – task should be completed with notes at this point and when applicable)
- Task to respond to Def. Disco (for assistant – task should be done at this point when applicable and based on firm's procedures)
- Task to file Motion for Extension of time to answer def. Disco and set for hearing (for paralegal – based on firm’s procedures and when applicable)
- Task to follow up with def. On plaintiff disco responses (for assistant and based on firm’s procedures)
- Task to do Motion to Compel Disco responses (for paralegal – based on firm’s procedures and when applicable)
- Task for plaintiff’s deposition (for scheduler – actively worked on and based on firm’s procedures)
- Task for plaintiff Deposition request (for scheduler – actively worked on and based on firm’s procedures)

5. **Deposition**

A [deposition](https://www.law.cornell.edu/wex/deposition) is a sworn out-of-court testimony given by a witness in the presence of a court reporter (person transcribing deposition discussion) requested by defendant’s lawyer. Note: please coordinate the Defendant’s deposition, it should take place on a date AFTER the Plaintiff is deposed but you can coordinate at the same time. Please refer to ‘’ Procedures for scheduling Deposition, Mediation and Conference Calls’ located on Documents/Clients/Clients/AA-Litigation Training Guide/Written procedures, to know how to schedule these.

- Task for def. Deposition request (for scheduler – more likely confirmed at this point but when applicable and based on firm’s procedures)
- Task for plaintiff’s deposition (for scheduler and based on firm’s procedures)
- Task to coordinate mediation or arbitration (for scheduler and based on firm’s procedures and any applicable CMP or Order from Court)

6. **Proposal for Settlement (PFS)**

This is a proposal any of the parties might make to try to resolve the case without the need to move the case further to mediation or trial. Plaintiff’s PFS should be filed after 91 days of service, Defendant’s can file PFS any time after they are served. **Deadline:** 30 days to respond, which applies to both parties.

- Task to draft & file PFS to Defendant’s (for paralegals and based on firm’s procedures – procedure pending)
- Task for PFS received from Defendant (for paralegals and based on firm’s procedures)

7. **Compulsory Medical Examination (CME)**

A defendant can request that the plaintiff attend a medical examination by the doctor of the defendant's choice. This is authorized by Florida law and Florida Rule of Civil Procedure 1.360. Usually, defense counsel requests a CME prior to Mediation. Note: If a CME is requested, client MUST comply with it as it is in compliant with Florida Statutes. If the client does not cooperate, the client might order the lawsuit to be dismissed for refusing to attend. *Please refer to ‘’Procedure – Compulsory Medical Examination’’*

- Task to coordinate the date (for the scheduler and based on firm’s procedures)
- Task to file response and objections, Agreed Order and potential MPO (for the paralegal and based on firm’s procedures)

8. **Arbitration/Mediation**
  1. Best attempt to settle prior to trial.
  2. Coordinate a mediator with opposing counsel, then coordinate a date.
  3. Schedule appointment with the mediator, calendar, and draft letter to client.
  4. Send client letter and reminders.
  5. Task Gilda to prep. the mediation binder (please give at least 3 weeks for her to prep.)

-Task to coordinate the arbitration or mediation (For scheduler and based on firm’s procedures)

- Task for arbitration ONLY to follow up on arbitration award and applicable motions (for paralegal and based on firm’s procedures – procedure pending update)

- Task for attorney’s legal assistant to draft Mediation binder or Arbitration report.

- Task for lien negotiator to review case for reductions / update net sheet

9. **Exhibit & Witness List**
  1. Needs to be drafted & filed.
  2. The expert witness deposition should be scheduled for a date after mediation (in the event we settle, the deposition is for use at trial) (more on this later)

- Task to draft & file exhibit, witness and expert witness list (for paralegals and based on firm’s procedures) - Procedure pending

- Task to coordinate expert witness deposition (for paralegal and based on firm’s procedures) - Procedure pending

- Task for expert witness discovery (for paralegals and based on firms’ procedures) - procedure pending

10. **Trial - (All tasks MUST be assigned to Paralegals)**
  1. If all attempts to settle fail, we go to trial. Must prep. trial binder.
  2. Must draft pretrial stipulation, jury instructions & jury verdict form.
  3. Once drafted, send it to your attorney to approve & then email it to opposing counsel in the event they want to make any changes. File.
  4. If/ when a case goes to trial, anything on the attorney’s calendar will need to be rescheduled.

- Task for calendar call and any docket sounding / pre-trial conference

- Task to draft pre-trial stipulation and Order.

- Task to draft jury instructions, jury verdict form and trial binder.

- Task for trial dates and to properly inform client of trial

title: New Hire Training Checklist: Personal Injury Team
summary: The documents to hand over and discuss with a new personal injury team member, the things to cover (notes, calls, Teams, tasks, updates) and tips to be successful.
body:
A checklist for a new member of the personal injury team. The supervisor goes through each document with the new hire and ticks it off.

### Documents to hand over and discuss

- PI Calls
- Case Phases Procedure
- Filevine Tasks Procedure
- Personal Injury Roles
- Naming Documents
- Welcome Call Procedure
- Documenting on Filevine and general information to remember
- 2-Week Call and Balance Verifications
- Treatment Case Review
- Pre-Demand Requirements
- Procedure on how to process invoices
- Withdraw and Terminated

### Things to discuss

- **How to document notes on Filevine.** Keep cases updated, in the correct phase, and well noted.
- **Calls.** The firm's process for incoming and outgoing calls. All calls must be returned within 24 business hours.
- **Teams.** Microsoft Teams must be on at all times and kept updated if team members are not available.
- **Tasks.** Stay up to date with tasks.
- **Updates.** Updates are sent through Teams and email. When an update is sent, team members must acknowledge that they read and understood it. If there are questions, tell the supervisor and ask for clarification. The firm is growing fast, so keeping up with changes is very important.
- **Emails.** The personal injury email and the personal injury internal email.

### Tips to be successful

- Time management and prioritizing are essential to succeed in the role.
- Run a report **every 2 weeks** (mandatory). Filter the cases by last contact and by phase.
- Check voicemails, emails and tasks daily so they do not pile up.
- Enter notes in Filevine while you are on the phone, to avoid doing the work twice.
- Know your numbers and expectations. Starting numbers are sent out monthly.
- Keep tasks to a minimum, and use the calendar in Filevine to keep track of important dates.

title: Personal Injury Calls: Who Takes Which Call
summary: Who is primary on a call by case phase, how to screen a potential new client call, and the call process: Teams chat, tasks and transfers.
body:
Use the case phases (see *Case Phases Procedure*) to know who a call should be transferred to, and who should be tasked and mentioned in the chat.

- The **legal assistants** are primary on cases in the initial phases, through Pre-Demand.
- The **case manager** is primary for calls from after the demand is sent until disbursement.
- If the team is not available, assign the task to the primary team member and write down the **name of the person who called, where they called from and their phone number**, so the call can be returned. Often, when a call goes to voicemail, the caller does not leave a number.

### PNC calls (potential new clients)

PNC calls are a priority and must be answered **immediately**. A PNC should never have to wait; a team member needs to respond. The intake coordinator is primary, but the whole team helps if the intake coordinator is not available.

Screening a PNC call, get:
- the full legal name (first, middle, last, and second last name if applicable)
- the referral source (how they heard about the firm)
- the type of accident (for example motor vehicle accident or workers' compensation)
- the preferred language (English or Spanish)
- a phone number

Post this information in the PI PNC chat. If there is no immediate response, include **@everyone**.

### Other important calls

The other important calls are clients calling, and adjusters calling when the case is in negotiations. Collection companies and other providers are not urgent most of the time.

### Who is primary?

**Legal assistant and case managers** are mentioned in Teams when the case is in one of these phases:
- Investigation
- File Set-Up
- Treatment
- Med Recs and Bills
- Pending Companion
- Pre-Demand
- Disbursements

**Case manager and attorney** are mentioned when the case is in one of these phases. There is a separate chat for cases in negotiations, since the attorneys are not in the PI incoming call chat.
- Liability Demand Sent
- Negotiations
- UM Negotiations
- UM Demand Sent
- Reductions

If a client is calling and a call-back task is more than **3 days overdue**, message the attorney or supervisor.

For cases in **Referred Out** or **Probate**, transfer the caller to the team member who works on referred-out and probate cases.

### Call process

1. When someone calls, add the information to the Teams chat and mention the legal team.
2. If there is no immediate response from the legal team, transfer the call to the appropriate team member and add a task for that team member.
3. If a team member does respond and asks for the call to be transferred, add a note that the call was transferred.
4. In every task, include the name of who called, where they called from and a call-back number.

title: Personal Injury Case Phases Procedure
summary: What each personal injury case phase means, from Investigation to Archived, how long a case should stay in each phase, and how to keep the phase tracker updated.
body:
### Overview

This procedure explains what each case phase means, so that every case is in the correct phase. Any time a case phase is changed in any project, the **Phase Tracker** must also be updated with the name of the team member who changed the phase and the date it was changed.

### Personal injury case phases

**Lead docket.** A case should not be in this phase. Once a case is transferred from the lead docket it is automatically put in this phase, and it must be changed to Investigation.

**Investigation.** A new case. The welcome call must be completed within 24 hours (see the *Welcome Call Procedure*). Follow up on this phase daily so the case moves to the next phase as soon as possible.
- We still need the police report and/or the insurance information (liability and UM) to file the claims and send out LORs right away.
- We also need the front and back of the health insurance card, to set up the subrogation claim, and a copy of the client's ID.
- Request the hospital discharge documents and the property damage pictures and/or PD estimate.
- This phase means the LORs have not been sent. A case should not be in this phase for longer than a week. The client should be set up for treatment, and we should have confirmed they are actively treating. **(1 week maximum)**

**File Set-Up.** LORs have been sent to liability, UM and health insurance.
- The boxes in the insurance section should be checked with the date the LORs were mailed. Copies of the LORs are saved in the correct provider section.
- File Set-Up means we are waiting for the declaration pages, confirming coverage and that liability has been accepted.
- We need BOTH the liability and the UM dec pages to move to the next phase. We can get verbal limits, but limits should not be entered, and the phase should not change, until we have the declaration pages.
- Follow up on the dec pages weekly. **(30 days; no more than 60 days)**

**Treatment.** The client is actively treating. Both declaration pages are saved, the limits are documented (liability and UM), and it is confirmed that the client is actively treating.
- The correct limits are entered in the insurance tab and confirmed by the case manager.
- Request the ER hospital records as soon as coverage and limits are confirmed. Do not wait until the client is done treating to request the hospital records and bills.
- We have also received correspondence from the health insurance.
- In this phase, contact the client every two weeks to check on them and their treatment status (see the *2-Week Call Procedure*). **(Varies depending on the injuries)**

**Med Recs / Bills.** The client has completed treatment. The client should confirm, preferably in writing by email or text, all the providers they treated with, so none is missed.
- We have requested records and itemized bills and are waiting for them.
- We have requested the updated health insurance explanation of benefits.
- Confirm lost wages and any examples of pain and suffering.
- Once the itemized bills are in, verify the balance with each provider (see the notes on how to verify balances). **(30 to 60 days from the day the client was released)**

**Pre-Demand.** Balances have been verified.
- The legal assistant called the adjuster and confirmed the adjuster's current mailing address where the demand should be mailed.
- We have the updated health insurance explanation of benefits and reviewed it to confirm we have all the providers the client treated with.
- We submitted the bills to the med pay adjuster and have the MPC EOB showing that med pay has been exhausted.
- We have all records, itemized bills, pictures and dec pages (see the *Pre-Demand Requirements checklist*).
- The legal assistant has completed and uploaded the pre-demand in the Demand/Negotiations bucket and tasked the case manager so the demand can be drafted. The attorney should be mentioned in the task.
- The order a case is prepared for demand: police report, pictures, bills, records, lost wages documentation.
- The declaration pages should also be saved in the insurance tab for the case manager to double-check before drafting the demand.
- The case manager or attorney also calls the client to get authorization to send the demand and to verify the providers again. The client is called with an update once the demand is mailed. **(1 week)**

**Pending Companion.** The client is done treating and the case is ready for a demand, but we are waiting for the companion case to draft and mail the demand. **(Varies case by case)**

**Returned to Treatment.** The client returned to treatment after the demand was sent.

**Liability Demand Sent.** The demand has been mailed. Track when it was delivered and set a calendar reminder for the case manager and attorney for 30 days after delivery to the adjuster. The negotiations tab is completed with the demand information, including the certified tracking information.

**Reductions / Pre-UM Demand.** Liability has tendered the policy limits, and the liability settlement is enough to pay the medicals. We can disburse on liability, and there is also UM exposure. We are working on reductions based on the amount received from liability. UM is available, so a UM demand will be sent.

**UM Demand Sent.** Track the demand and set a calendar reminder for the case manager and attorney for 60 days after the demand was delivered to the adjuster. The client needs to be called and updated.

**Negotiation.** The demand has been received and the adjuster has made an offer. The offer is documented in the negotiations tab. **(45 days from the first offer)**

**UM Negotiations.** The UM demand was sent and we are negotiating. **(45 days from the first offer)**

**Reductions.** We have received a final offer and the case has settled. We are working on the reductions to get the final case amount and the final reduction approval.
- Note every reduction request and approval on each provider.
- Send reductions as soon as possible to avoid delays. **(30 days)**

**Need Check.** The case has settled, the reductions are done, and the client has signed the exit letter and release. We are only waiting for the settlement check so we can disburse. The case manager and attorney follow up with the adjuster on the status of the settlement check.

**Accounting.** Exit packets are completed and given to the accounting department to write the checks.

**Disbursement.** Checks have been received from accounting and are being disbursed.

**Closing.** All checks have been mailed to the providers, and the settlement check was given or mailed to the client. Accounting monitors that all the checks have cleared. Once all have cleared, the case is moved to Archive.

**Litigation Review.** The case is being reviewed for possible litigation.

**Pre-Suit.** We are waiting to file suit, either because the suit is being drafted or because it has been drafted and is waiting for attorney review and approval. **(30 days)**

**Pending Service.** We filed suit and are waiting for the defendant(s) to be served. **(15 days; calendar it if not completed within 15 days with the process server)**

**Answer.** The defendant(s) have been served and we are waiting for them to file an answer. **(45 days from the date of service; it is calendared)**

**Discovery.** We are exchanging discovery and depositions. **(6 months from the defendant's answer)**

**Pending Trial.** Discovery is over and we are waiting for trial. **(Depends on the court; could be 6 months to a year or longer)**

**Worker's Comp.** A workers' compensation case. The name of the attorney it was referred to is added as a hashtag and in the case summary tab.

**Wrongful Death.** Not really used. Add the **#wrongfuldeath** hashtag to wrongful death cases and use the phases listed above that apply, for example File Set-Up, Demand Sent or Negotiations.

**Referred Out.** The case was referred to another attorney.

**Archived.** The case has been settled or closed and all checks have cleared.

### Time allowed for each phase

| Phase | Time allowed |
|---|---|
| Investigation | 1 week maximum |
| File Set-Up | 60 days |
| Medical Records and Bills | 60 days |
| Pre-Demand | 15 days |
| Liability Demand Sent | Over 45 days |
| Negotiations | 30 days |
| Reductions | 30 days |
| UM Demand Sent | Over 75 days |
| Disbursement | Over 30 days |
| Need Check | 30 days |
| Treatment | Varies with the severity of the injuries and the treatment (the 2-week contact calls are reviewed) |

title: Filevine Tasks and Notes Procedure
summary: How to write notes in the right bucket, assign and complete tasks, avoid duplicate tasks and attach the right documents.
body:
### Overview

This procedure explains how to assign and complete tasks properly, and how to write notes in specific areas. Tasks and notes keep cases worked efficiently.

### Notes

- **All notes go in the Activity section, in the matching bucket** (see the buckets procedure). Notes in the buckets are time and date stamped, and only the original author can change them.
- Notes can be copied and pasted into the matching tabs, such as Negotiations, an individual medical provider, Billable Expenses or an individual insurance company. These notes let everyone know when something has been done, so tasks are not duplicated.
- **There must be a note in the bucket any time a task is assigned.** When you write a note for a specific section (meds, insurance, billable expenses or negotiations), write the date, your note (you can copy and paste it from the activity section) and your initials.
- **The most recent note always goes at the top.**

**Format:** (date) (task information) (initials).
**Example:** *8/17/23 - Assigned a task to a team member to follow up on the liability dec page. (initials)*

**Example:** A task is assigned to a team member in the "Liability Insurance" bucket to follow up on the liability dec page. The person then goes to the insurance tab and notes that the task was assigned. This keeps the same task from being assigned to someone else, and because the task is assigned outside the bucket, the notes keep accurate information on when the task was assigned and when it was completed.

When the team member receives the dec page, they check off the task and write a note in the matching bucket.

### Tasks

- **Do not re-use tasks.** Re-using a task creates inaccurate task completion times.
- **Assign tasks outside of the buckets AND write a note in the bucket** saying that you assigned the task.
- **When a task is completed, check it off as completed** and enter a note that refers to the bucket for the detailed notes, if applicable.
  - *Example:* On a client call-back task, write "See client call bucket" when it is completed. The detailed notes of the conversation go in the client call bucket.
- **A task can be assigned in a bucket only once.** If a task was already assigned, whether complete or not, assign a new task outside the bucket and write a note in the bucket that a task was assigned. This avoids several people working on the same task.
  - *Example:* A team member needs to assign a task to follow up on the hospital records, but a previous task was assigned to someone else to follow up on the ortho records. She writes a note in the bucket saying she assigned a task to follow up on the hospital records. Once that person follows up, they check off the task and write a detailed note, "See Treatment / Recs and Bills bucket", where the detailed notes are.

### Assigning several tasks at once

When you assign a task for several things, such as filing a UM claim, a liability claim and a subrogation claim, **assign one task in each matching bucket** and attach any documents that help the team member complete it.

- *Example:* If a VA is to file the liability claim and the UM claim, assign one task in the liability bucket and another in the UM bucket, with the police report attached if it is available. This keeps track of all the tasks completed during the day.
- If a task is to request hospital records and bills, attach the **discharge documents**.
- If a task is to file the health insurance subrogation, include the **front and back of the health insurance card**.

title: Personal Injury Roles: Virtual Assistant, Legal Assistant and Case Manager
summary: What the virtual assistant, the legal assistant and the case manager each do in a personal injury case, by phase, plus the team meetings.
body:
### Virtual Assistant

- File claims and generate LORs (liability and UM).
- Generate subrogation LORs.
- Request hospital medical records and bills and follow up until they arrive. It is the legal assistant's and case manager's responsibility to make sure the specific hospital was given to the VA. Task every two weeks.
- Verify balances.
- Call adjusters to verify the current adjuster contact information for the pre-demand.
- Follow up on the status of dec pages and get verbal limits.
- Name documents on file.
- Complete the tasks assigned to the team.
- Translate.

### Legal Assistant

**Phases: Investigation to Pre-Demand.**
- Complete welcome calls.
- Name documents on file.
- Obtain the police report and assign a task to the VA to file claims. Cases should not be in the Investigation phase for longer than a week.
- Mail out LORs once they are generated. Follow up on dec pages.
- Make the 2-week calls.
- Keep the medical providers updated in the meds tab.
- Get the updated health insurance EOB.
- Update the dates of service once the bills and records are received.
- **Update the treatment status.**
- Complete the health insurance questionnaire and return it to the analyst, or call.
- Follow up with the client for missing information (ID, health insurance, hospital discharge documents).
- Provide updates to providers. Confirm that the client gets an MRI within the first month of the case.
- Send med pay demands.
- **Pay invoices and confirm they are not duplicates.** Document all invoices and expenses in the billable expenses and save them in the document bucket.
- Task the case manager to review the dec pages, and enter the limits once the case manager has reviewed the dec page.
- Send HIPAA authorizations to the providers the firm works with, so medical records and bills can be obtained.
- Bring any issues to the case manager's attention right away.
- Follow up on medical records and bills.
- Make sure cases are in the correct phase.
- Task virtual assistants with miscellaneous tasks.
- Complete the pre-demand package and task the case manager once it is complete for review.
- Mail disbursement checks and demands.
- Complete tasks assigned by the case manager.
- **Task the case manager before changing a case from Treatment to Med Recs and Bills.**

### Case Manager

**Phases: Investigation to Med Recs.** Oversee that the case is being built up and help the legal assistant with anything needed.
**Phases: Pre-Demand to Disbursement.**

- Review all new cases within 24 hours and assign notes for the legal assistant about the welcome call. Identify high-value cases, or cases that can settle quickly (severity of injuries, hospital treatment for days, broken bones).
- Review that the case was set up correctly, by putting all parties on notice right away (UM primary, secondary, defendant) and sending an open records request when needed.
- Review spoliation letters before the attorney reviews them.
- Review the providers where the client is treating. Confirm the medical providers are listed correctly in the meds tab. Confirm that the client is scheduled for an MRI in the first month and is seeing an MD. Build up the case.
- Review the cases in Investigation once a week to make sure we have the information needed to send the LOR.
- Review invoices to confirm they are not duplicates. Contact the records vendor or the providers to cancel duplicate invoices.
- Name documents on file.
- Talk to clients before a case changes from Treatment to Medical Records and Bills, to make sure the client is done treating (check treatment, policy limits, property damage).
- Bring issues to the attorneys' attention after the case manager has tried to resolve them first.
- Verify that the welcome call was made, and give the legal assistant information to ask clients within 24 hours after the welcome call was assigned. Add notes when cases are reviewed in the Onboarding bucket (see the onboarding call procedure).
- Check cases in the Treatment phase at least once a month, to make sure the clients are being called and the case is being worked correctly.
- Complete VIP welcome calls, and review the file before the legal assistant makes the welcome call, to find any issues or specific questions the legal assistant should ask.
- Make sure cases are in the correct phase.
- Review the pre-demand to make sure the legal assistant completed all steps: med pay exhausted, balances verified, providers verified, adjuster contact information verified, and all records and bills on file.
- Draft demands.
- Send releases to adjusters and save them in the exit bucket.
- Help the attorneys with lien searches. Attorneys should also check for liens, and all searches should be saved in the case management system and the document bucket.
- Help the attorney with negotiations (follow up on checks and releases).
- Complete reductions right away.
- Complete the case summary and the final settlement information in the case management system.
- Complete exit letters, and keep track of the numbers (settlements, demands written, cases settled).
- Do a lien search, or confirm that the attorneys completed the lien search, before disbursement.
- Update the PI board.

### Meetings

- The supervisor meets with the team by the **17th of every month** to go over cases and see whether the team is on track to meet its goal.
- The legal assistant and case manager meet briefly **once a week** to plan the week.
- The case manager and attorney meet **once a month** to go over cases, focusing on VIP cases and reviewing statute of limitations cases.

### Notes

- During the welcome call, the team adds the **#hospital** hashtag, or enters a note in the Treatment bucket saying that the client did not treat at the hospital.
- **Case summary:** the settlement summary is completed within **60 days**, with the projected settlement date and the projected settlement goal.

title: Naming Documents and Case Folders
summary: How to name every document so it can be found, and what goes in each personal injury case subfolder, including criminal and workers' compensation matters.
body:
### Naming documents

Everything the firm receives must be **named in the case management system and in the shared document folders**. The items in the shared folders are named the same way as they are saved in the case management system.

Every description should include the **client's last name(s), first name and middle name**.

**Examples**
- State Farm liability dec page - (client's last names, first name, middle name)
- AICA medical records and $999 bill - (client's name)
- PP-CIOX $149.50 Northside Hosp records - (client's name)
- Signed Completed Exit Packet - (client's name)
- Signed WC contract - (client's name)
- Final Disposition - (client's name)

### Personal injury folders (subfolders of the case folder)

| Folder | What goes in it |
|---|---|
| **Onboarding** | Contract, ID, front and back of the health insurance card, HIPAA authorization, and any information obtained during onboarding. |
| **Correspondence** | Any correspondence received about the case: letters of acknowledgement, health insurance correspondence and questionnaire, case update requests from adjusters. |
| **Ins. Dec pages** | The liability and UM dec pages, including the signed UM selection form. |
| **Medical Records / Bills** | All medical records and itemized bills for the case. |
| **Lost Wages** | The lost wages form and the tax document that supports lost wages if the client is self-employed. |
| **Evidence** | Videos, pictures, the police report, or any other evidence for the case. |
| **Expenses** | Any expense related to the case, for example the police report, intake fee, postage, and invoices for medical records and bills. |
| **Demand** | A copy of the entire demand: liability, UM and med pay. |
| **Reductions** | All reduction requests and reduction approvals. |
| **Exit** | All exit packets and the documents that close the case. |

### Miscellaneous folder: criminal and workers' compensation cases

**Criminal subfolders**
- **Onboarding:** contract, ID, police report.
- **Evidence:** evidence related to the case.
- **Court Documents:** all court documents.
- **Exit:** all documents confirming the case is closed, and the final disposition form.

**Workers' compensation subfolders**
- **Onboarding:** the contract with the other attorney, and any documents the client provided during intake.
- **Exit:** the settlement check, once we receive it from the attorney.

title: Welcome Call Procedure
summary: How to complete the welcome call within 24 hours: the contact card, what to confirm (insurance, injuries, prior claims, bankruptcy, lost wages, social media) and what to tell the client.
body:
### Overview

The purpose of this procedure is to make sure every welcome call is completed correctly.

### General guidelines

- A welcome call must be completed as soon as the team (legal assistant, case manager and attorney) is notified of the new case, and **within 24 hours** after being notified. The team is notified of a new case through the Teams PNC chat, a task and an email.
- In the **Project Vitals** section, add **#Spanishspeaker** or **#Englishspeaker**. Add **#hospital** if the client went to the hospital.
- **Notes:** welcome call notes go in the **Onboarding** bucket.
- The welcome call task is checked off by the attorney and the case manager or legal assistant once the call is complete.
- If the legal assistant completes the call, the case manager reviews the case and lets the legal assistant know if specific information is needed. The case manager reviews the severity of the injuries and whether the client went to the ER.

### The contact card

**Contact Info tab.** The client's full legal name, date of birth, mailing address (including the apartment number if applicable), phone number and email. A copy of the ID needs to be saved to the contact card.
- The contact type is completed as "client". If the client was a passenger, add that next to the client's name. If the client has had several accidents we represent them for, add the date of the accident at the top next to the client's name.

**Details tab.** Gender, marital status, driver's license number, the language the client speaks, and the client's SSN.
- If the client does not have an SSN or refuses to give it, enter 000-000-0000. Also write a note in the "Notes" section, and the client must sign the CMS form or the affidavit that they are not Medicare or Medicaid eligible.

**Client Journey tab.** Check the "Address verified" box once the address has been verified, and enter the date it was verified. If there are companions on the case, we need their names and their relationship to the client.

### What to confirm and collect on the call

**Emergency contact.** Every case should have an emergency contact. Also get written confirmation if the client authorizes us to disclose detailed information to anyone, including their spouse or emergency contact. The emergency contact is in the PI Intake tab under **Personal Info**.

**Obtain missing information.** Intake asks the client for important case information. If something has not been received, follow up on it. Documents needed:
- ID or driver's license
- police report number or the police report
- front and back of the health insurance card
- pictures of any visible injuries
- the estimate of the property damage
- pictures of the client's and the defendant's property damage
- any discharge documents from places where the client has already treated
- emergency contact information, in case we cannot reach the client

**Insurance.** Ask whether the client has personal insurance, or any other car insurance that may not be listed on the police report. Ask whether they have a **resident relative** and explain what a resident relative is.

**Injuries.** Confirm all injuries and update them in the PI Intake tab under **Injuries**. Think from head to toe. It is extremely important to list every injury.
- Screen the client for a possible **TBI**: any sensitivity to light or noise, dizziness, headaches, nausea, mood swings, or being easily irritated? If so, refer them to a neurologist for a proper diagnosis.
- It is important that the client does not see only a chiropractor and does get seen by an MD. If the injuries are severe, do not send the client to a chiropractor.

**Prior injuries.** Does the client have a prior injury that could have been aggravated by the new accident? Ask whether they have had prior claims and injuries. If so, we need to know when they were injured, how severe the prior injuries were, and whether they hired an attorney. If they did, do they remember whom they hired and how much they received? Depending on the answers, we may need to obtain the file from the prior accident. Complete the **Priors** section (prior injuries, prior lawsuits with an attorney, prior claims, prior bankruptcy).

**Bankruptcy.** Has the client filed for bankruptcy? If so, has it been discharged or is it still active? If it has not been discharged, we need to know whether it was Chapter 7 or 13, and we need the bankruptcy attorney's contact information. Let the attorney or supervisor know about an active bankruptcy case. If the bankruptcy is closed or discharged, write a note; no further action is needed.

**Lost wages.** Has the client lost wages because of the injuries? Send the lost wages (LW) form to the client by email and add it to the meds tab. Add the lost wages information in the Meds tab. If the client says they did not lose wages and will not, add that note in the lost wages section. Complete the **Economic Damages** section of the PI Intake tab (employment status, notes, concurrent employment, tax returns).

**Social media.** Remind the client that what they post online, or are tagged in, may be used against them. Complete the information in the PI Intake tab under **Wrap-Up** (reviewed the social media letter or policy, concerns raised, all social media platforms and user IDs).

### Reminders for the client

- Explain the process and what to expect. Confirm the client has received the legal assistant's and the attorney's contact information, and the PI intro video.
- They should discuss only things related to the property damage with the adjuster. The client should **not give a recorded statement** without speaking with the attorney or legal assistant.
- Be careful with what they post, discuss or are tagged in on social media.
- Keep track of, and give us, examples of non-economic damages (pain and suffering).
- Remind them again how important it is to treat consistently with no gaps in treatment. Confirm the client has been scheduled for treatment.

### After the call

Go to the **Case Summary** tab and enter the date the call was completed. The tab has a section for the attorney and for the person who completed the welcome call (the case manager or the legal assistant). The client contact dates are: attorney initial 24-hour call, legal assistant initial 24-hour call, case manager initial 24-hour call, most recent client contact, and most recent attempted contact.

title: Documenting in the Case System: Insurance and Meds Tabs
summary: How to complete the contact cards, the insurance tab (liability, UM, health, resident relative, med pay) and the meds tab, including hospital bills and pre-settlement loans.
body:
- **All information in the Intake and Case Summary tabs should be completed.** Intake gets as much information as it can, but it is the legal assistant's responsibility to confirm information and obtain what is missing. The welcome call is for confirming information and getting what is missing, for example: legal name, marital status, date of birth, Social Security number, copy of ID, copy of the front and back of the health insurance card, spouse information, emergency contact, previous accidents or claims, injured body parts, bankruptcy, child support and employment status.
- **Contact cards should always be completed.** Full legal name, date of birth, driver's license number if you have it (usually on the police report), phone number, email, fax, mailing address and so on, for **all clients, adjusters, defendants and providers**.
- **Most recent attempt and most recent contact** must be updated every time we attempt, or have a successful contact with, the client. If the client does not answer, send a text message and a follow-up email.

### Insurance tab

The insurance tab should **always have at least three rows**. There are statutes of limitations on filing claims, so if they are not filed on time, coverage could be denied.

1. Insurance tab: **Liability**
2. **UM insurance**
3. **Health insurance**
4. If the client is a passenger, we need **their personal insurance**, since it is primary.
5. If there is a **resident relative**, add the resident relative's name, relationship to the client, policy number and the name of the insurance company.

**Rules to remember**
- **Personal car insurance is primary.** If a client is a passenger in a vehicle, that vehicle's UM is secondary. **UM follows the person.**
- **Med pay follows the car, not the person.**
- Ask clients whether they have a resident relative, which could help increase the value of the case if the relative has UM.
- Add the health insurance information. If there is no health insurance, add a note saying so. Save a copy of the front and back of the health insurance card and a copy of the LOR. Follow up and get the health insurance EOB.
- If the client is a passenger or a driver, specify it next to the client's name in the project.
